2f1be15a0d4f0228: KOTA TINGGI: The additional costs of equipping the Royal Malaysian Navy's (RMN) littoral combat ships (LCS) with Türkiye's Atmaca missiles will cover integration work and the provision of launch systems.

Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said the government had already ordered Atmaca missiles for its littoral mission ships (LMS), allowing part of the existing order to be redirected to the LCS as a replacement for Norway's Naval Strike Missile (NSM).
"I have already ordered Atmaca missiles for the LMS. So now, I only need to take those Atmaca missiles and put them there (on the LCS).

"The additional costs will be for integration and the launch systems. Once Norway refunds our money, we will use it to pay for the new missiles," he told reporters after attending the Sekolah Angkat Madani handover ceremony at Sekolah Kebangsaan Panchor here today.
Khaled said the Atmaca missiles ordered for the LMS were expected to be ready in 2028, adding that using the same system would allow the ministry to utilise its existing order.
He declined to disclose the additional costs, saying negotiations were ongoing.
Asked whether the government was confident of recovering the payment from Norway, Khaled said the process could involve legal action, including arbitration or court proceedings.

"If we go for arbitration, many parties do not comply with arbitration decisions. They may also refuse to comply, and we may have to go to court. It could take two, three, four or five years. I do not know," he said.

The government had earlier selected Türkiye as an alternative supplier to replace the NSM system after evaluating proposals from several countries, including France and Italy, based on price, delivery timelines and upfront costs.
Khaled said further negotiations would be held with Türkiye to finalise the procurement, including ensuring the missile system's suitability for and integration with the LCS.

On May 19, the Defence Ministry issued a notice of claim against Norwegian defence manufacturer Kongsberg Defence & Aerospace AS, seeking about RM1 billion in compensation following the cancellation of the NSM export permit.
The amount comprises €126 million (RM583.47 million) in direct costs already paid by the government, as well as claims for indirect losses.
b4fb0938d3a6d763: KUALA LUMPUR: Rexy Mainaky has called for patience with the national mixed doubles squad following their recent poor results.
The national doubles coaching director said the BA of Malaysia (BAM) pairs were still adapting to different coaching methods following former head coach Nova Widianto's departure in July.
Rexy is currently overseeing the department, with help from Teo Kok Siang and Pang Cheh Chang.
"We have to look at the transition following Nova's departure. There are new ideas from the coaches, and Kok Siang and Cheh Chang are handling the squad at the moment," said Rexy.
"A transition takes time. We hope the players can adapt quickly, but there has been a change of coach and a different approach."
BAM's mixed doubles pairs have struggled for consistency since June, with Jimmy Wong-Cheng Su Yin's Japan Open semi-final appearance among the few bright spots.
The latest setback came at this week's Kumamoto Masters, where Jimmy-Su Yin and Chen Tang Jie-Chan Wen Tse were eliminated in the first round on Wednesday.
World No. 32 Jimmy-Su Yin lost 21-8, 23-21 to China's world No. 6 Guo Xin Wa-Chen Fang Hui, while Tang Jie-Wen Tse fell 21-15, 21-10 to Japan's Yuichi Shimogami-Sayaka Hobara.
For Jimmy-Su Yin, it was a third consecutive opening-round defeat following similar exits at the Denmark and French Opens.
They reached the Arctic Open last 16 before the two European tournaments, but have been unable to build on their Japan Open breakthrough in July and Korea Masters quarter-final appearance in August.
Tang Jie-Wen Tse, meanwhile, have yet to reach a quarter-final in four tournaments together after last-16 finishes at the Arctic, Denmark and Korea Opens.
Tang Jie has been competing with different partners since regular partner Toh Ee Wei suffered a knee injury at the Singapore Open in May.
Rexy said Ee Wei's absence was another factor to consider alongside the coaching transition.
Nova left BAM on July 31 to return to Indonesia, ending a stint that began in January 2023 and included guiding Tang Jie-Ee Wei to Malaysia's first mixed doubles world title in Paris last year.
Kok Siang returned to the national set-up on Sept 1 as a mixed doubles coach, after serving in BAM's junior and senior doubles programmes before leaving in 2022.
ddcf989875590906: MELAKA, Nov 14 — More than 50 per cent of registered voters in Melaka had cast their ballots by 1.38pm today, passing the halfway mark in the state election.
The Election Commission’s (EC) real-time Voter Turnout Monitoring dashboard recorded turnout at 50.43 per cent as of 1.38pm, with 337,716 voters having voted.
The EC is targeting a 70 per cent turnout in the election, which sees 79 candidates contesting 28 seats.
Serkam continued to record the highest turnout among the 28 state constituencies, at 57.19 per cent, while Bandar Hilir was the lowest, at 43.16 per cent.
Serkam was closely followed by Tanjung Bidara at 56.55 per cent, Ayer Molek at 55.93 per cent and Ayer Limau at 55.73 per cent.
A total of 240 polling centres, comprising 1,213 polling streams, opened at 8am today for the 16th Melaka state election.
Voting is scheduled to continue until 6pm, following the end of the 14-day campaign period at 11.59pm last night.
The EC said 675,166 ordinary voters are eligible to cast their ballots in the election.
The total number of registered voters is 687,697, including 12,531 military personnel, their spouses and police personnel who were eligible to vote during the early voting phase on Tuesday.
Early voting was conducted at 31 polling centres, with 9,417 of the 9,917 eligible voters casting their ballots in person, representing a turnout of 94.96 per cent.
Another 2,614 voters cast their ballots by post.

Pakatan Harapan (PH) is fielding the most candidates, contesting 24 seats, followed by Barisan Nasional (BN) with 23, Parti Bersama Malaysia with 16, Parti Pribumi Perkasa Malaysia (Putra) with one and three independents.

Bersatu, a component of Perikatan Nasional (PN), is contesting seven seats under its own logo this time, separate from PN’s five candidates, who comprise two each from PAS and Parti Wawasan Negara and one from Gerakan.
The 79 candidates were confirmed following the nomination process on October 31.
The election follows the dissolution of the 15th Melaka State Legislative Assembly on September 23, with the consent of Yang di-Pertua Negeri Tun Mohd Ali Rustam.
In the previous state election on November 20, 2021, BN won 21 of the 28 seats, PH took five and Bersatu secured two under the BN banner.

4964ac8da78359a7: NOVEMBER 14 — The events of November 13, 2026, have demonstrated how vulnerable even the world’s most technologically advanced country can be.
The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) ordered a nationwide ground stop lasting more than four hours. Thousands of flights were delayed or cancelled.
International aviation was disrupted, leaving passengers stranded far beyond American shores.
The crisis occurred in the same week as a major Microsoft systems outage affecting businesses and public institutions.
Yet American officials have indicated that the two incidents were unrelated.
Preliminary findings pointed towards ageing aviation technology and telecommunications failures rather than a malicious cyberattack.
This is precisely why evidence must prevail over speculation.
The coincidence of two technological failures does not prove that they share the same cause. Neither does the scale of the disruption automatically establish foreign interference.

Indeed, if the United States, with its immense technological resources, can suffer such systemic failures, Washington must exercise considerable humility before attributing similar disruptions elsewhere to hostile powers.
The same principle applies to the extraordinary controversy surrounding Jensen Huang, the former chief executive officer of Nvidia.
Huang resigned on November 11 following revelations concerning extramarital relationships, including reported affairs involving two Nvidia employees.
Reports have also linked him romantically to Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman whom American intelligence officials reportedly suspected of espionage.
However, suspicion is not proof.

There has been no publicly established finding demonstrating that Alice Huang was acting as a Chinese intelligence operative. Nor has it been established that Jensen Huang knowingly transferred sensitive American technology to Chinese intelligence.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Flowers rest at an Nvidia sign displayed outside the company’s headquarters on November 12, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. — AFP pic
The distinction is enormously important.

Huang’s reported relationships with Nvidia employees raise legitimate questions about corporate ethics, conflicts of interest and the standards expected of the chief executive of one of the world’s most valuable corporations.
These are serious governance issues that warrant independent investigation.
But corporate misconduct and espionage are not interchangeable accusations.
To treat an unproven allegation of espionage as established fact risks turning a corporate scandal into a geopolitical confrontation between the United States and China.
Nvidia had approached a market valuation of US$5 trillion before its dramatic decline.
Following Huang’s resignation, its valuation stood at approximately US$4 trillion, with its shares having fallen substantially since their early October peak.
Although the scandal surrounding Huang contributed to investor uncertainty, the broader decline cannot be attributed entirely to his personal conduct.

Questions concerning artificial intelligence valuations, capital expenditure, geopolitical restrictions and the sustainability of demand for advanced semiconductors have also affected market confidence.
It would therefore be analytically irresponsible to explain the entire collapse in Nvidia’s market value through one man’s personal affairs.
For Asean, these developments are not merely American domestic affairs.
The United States and China are two indispensable economic partners of Southeast Asia.
American technology companies remain central to Asean’s digital transformation.
Chinese manufacturing, trade and investment networks are equally important to the region’s economic development.
The semiconductor industry illustrates this interdependence.
Malaysia, Singapore and Vietnam occupy important positions in global electronics and semiconductor supply chains.
Any deterioration in US-China technological relations can affect investment decisions, export controls and the availability of advanced computing systems.
The allegation that a Chinese businesswoman may have engaged in espionage through her relationship with an American technology executive therefore has implications extending far beyond Nvidia.
If the allegations are substantiated through credible investigations, the appropriate legal and regulatory consequences should follow.
But if they remain unproven, neither Washington nor Beijing should allow them to become another source of strategic hostility.
Asean has every reason to encourage both powers to maintain transparent procedures, reliable communication channels and institutional safeguards against premature attribution.
This is especially important as artificial intelligence increasingly becomes central to national security.
A rules-based order must apply to everyone
A rules-based international order cannot mean that powerful countries are entitled to make accusations while weaker countries must provide evidence.
Rules must apply consistently.
They must govern the conduct of governments, intelligence agencies, multinational corporations and international institutions.
The principle of due process is not merely a domestic legal safeguard. It also provides an important foundation for international confidence.
Countries cannot be expected to cooperate when allegations are repeatedly treated as conclusions.
Neither can technological interdependence survive indefinitely if commercial relationships are automatically interpreted through the lens of espionage.

The United States has legitimate concerns about protecting its advanced technologies. China has legitimate interests in ensuring that its businesses and citizens are not subjected to unfounded accusations.
Asean, meanwhile, has legitimate interests in maintaining productive relations with both.
These interests need not be mutually exclusive.
The challenge is to establish procedures through which genuine security threats can be investigated without transforming every controversy into another episode of great-power rivalry.
The Trump administration has repeatedly emphasised military strength, technological superiority and the protection of American strategic interests.
Yet the aviation disruptions of November 13 illustrate the limitations of relying excessively on power.
No number of aircraft carriers can substitute for reliable air traffic control systems.
No amount of military expenditure can automatically prevent the failure of ageing telecommunications infrastructure.
Similarly, the possession of the world’s most advanced artificial intelligence chips does not guarantee the integrity of corporate governance.
Power without institutional resilience can become surprisingly fragile.
For this reason, the United States and Asean should broaden and deepen their strategic cooperation beyond conventional defence arrangements.
Their relationship must encompass aviation safety, cybersecurity, digital infrastructure, artificial intelligence governance and mechanisms for investigating major technological disruptions.
This requires technical cooperation between regulators, universities, research institutes and private companies.
It also requires diplomatic dialogue capable of separating legitimate national security concerns from politically convenient allegations.
Asean should not be reduced to choosing between Washington and Beijing.
Rather, Asean should strengthen its capacity to insist that both powers observe internationally acceptable standards of evidence, transparency and accountability.
The importance of the Asean will
The Philippines, as Asean Chair in 2026, has an opportunity to reinforce these principles.
The Asean-US Comprehensive Strategic Partnership should increasingly incorporate evidence-based mechanisms for addressing technological and security controversies.
An Asean-US dialogue on critical infrastructure resilience would be a constructive starting point.
Such cooperation could examine the vulnerabilities of aviation systems, telecommunications networks, data centres and semiconductor supply chains.
It could also establish procedures for sharing technical findings following major disruptions without prematurely assigning blame.
Asean should simultaneously encourage similar cooperation with China, Japan, South Korea and other dialogue partners.
This is not an exercise in geopolitical neutrality for its own sake.

It is the practical expression of the Asean Will: the collective determination of South-east Asian countries to protect their strategic autonomy through cooperation, institutional competence and principled diplomacy.
The region must avoid becoming an arena in which unverified accusations between major powers produce economic and security consequences for countries that had no role in the original controversy.
From speculation to strategic stability
The United States and China possess sufficient scientific and technological expertise to understand the dangers of uncontrolled escalation.
Both are aware that artificial intelligence, advanced semiconductors and digital infrastructure are increasingly intertwined with national security.
But precisely because these technologies are so sensitive, allegations concerning their misuse require exceptional evidentiary discipline.
The danger is not simply that a false accusation might damage an individual’s reputation.
It is that an unproven allegation can be amplified through political rhetoric, financial markets and intelligence assessments until it begins to shape national policy.
By that stage, even a subsequent correction may not reverse the diplomatic damage.
Asean must therefore advocate a rules-based international order in which verification precedes accusation, investigation precedes punishment and dialogue precedes confrontation.
The November aviation crisis demonstrates that even the strongest country can be humbled by technological fragility.

64aac26c57b1de43: KUALA LUMPUR: Four Olympic appearances have given Khairulnizam Afendy plenty of experience at the highest level, but the national sailor now wants to use that knowledge to help develop the next generation.
The 33-year-old, who competed at the 2012 London, 2016 Rio, 2020 Tokyo and 2024 Paris Olympics, will captain Malaysian Monsoon at the SSL Gold Cup in Rio de Janeiro.
Khairulnizam also won Asian Games silver medals at the 2014 Incheon and 2018 Jakarta-Palembang editions before claiming bronze at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games.
He said his motivation had evolved beyond personal achievements, with the SSL Gold Cup providing an opportunity to give back to Malaysian sailing.

"After representing Malaysia at four Olympic Games, my motivation is no longer just about personal achievements. I want to give something back to Malaysian sailing by sharing my experience and helping develop the next generation," he said.
The SSL Gold Cup presents a different challenge from his individual ILCA 7 campaign, where he is responsible for making decisions on the water.
"In ILCA 7, I depend on myself and make all the decisions on the water. In the SSL Gold Cup, success depends on every crew member doing their job.
"As captain, my role is to bring everyone together, build trust and maintain good communication. We need to understand each other's strengths and work as one team," he said.
Malaysia will be looking to improve on their 2023 campaign in Gran Canaria, where Malaysian Monsoon finished top ten overall.
Khairulnizam believes the previous campaign provided valuable experience and a better understanding of the competition, although he acknowledged that the challenge in Rio would be demanding.
"Our previous campaign gave us valuable experience and showed that Malaysia can challenge some of the strongest sailing nations. We understand the level of competition much better now.

"Of course, it will not be easy, but we are coming to Rio with confidence and a strong fighting spirit. Our target is to go beyond the quarter-finals and see how far we can take Malaysian Monsoon," he said.
A podium finish would be a historic achievement for Malaysian sailing, and Khairulnizam believes a team success would carry a special meaning after his individual accomplishments at the Olympics.

"Reaching the podium would be a historic moment for Malaysian sailing and prove that we can compete with the best in the world. Most importantly, I want to inspire the younger generation to dream bigger and believe that Malaysian sailors can achieve great things on the international stage," he said.
The 2026 SSL Gold Cup, featuring 66 nations competing on identical SSL47 yachts, takes place in Guanabara Bay, Rio de Janeiro, from Nov 19 to Dec 13.
Khairulnizam also thanked the team's sponsors, stakeholders and the Raja Muda Selangor, Tengku Amir Shah Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah, for their continued support in making the trip possible.
9d0a6d15ccdf19ed: MANILA, Nov 14 — A Philippine court has ordered the arrest of a jailed preacher sought by Washington for alleged child sex trafficking, a step toward his possible extradition to the United States, Manila said today.

Self-proclaimed “Son of God” Apollo Quiboloy is currently being held without bail in a Philippine prison while on trial for a separate charge of human trafficking, which carries life in prison if convicted.
Manila filed a petition with a lower court on Monday to authorise his extradition to the United States, Philippine justice department spokesman Polo Martinez told AFP.

On Thursday, the court issued an extradition warrant of arrest against Quiboloy and two female associates — both at large — “after finding probable cause that each extraditee committed the offence or offences charged,” Martinez added.
Under Philippine law, the court must now hold hearings before a final decision is made on the transfer.
Quiboloy, an ally of former president Rodrigo Duterte, was arrested in 2024 and later pleaded not guilty to the Philippine charges.
A US grand jury separately indicted Quiboloy in 2021 for conspiracy to engage in sex trafficking by force, fraud and coercion, sex trafficking of children and bulk cash smuggling.
The US indictment alleges women were recruited as personal assistants for Quiboloy, said to be in his mid-70s, to prepare his meals, clean his residence, give him massages and have sex with him.
Washington formally sought his extradition in August.

Martinez, the justice department spokesman, told AFP the Philippine court also issued a separate “hold departure order” against Quiboloy and his two associates to “prevent any attempt by each of them to depart from the Philippines”.
Quiboloy’s Kingdom of Christ sect claims millions of followers in the mainly Catholic Asian nation and owns a television network.
He was allowed to run for Senate in the country’s 2025 midterm elections despite his incarceration and garnered 5.6 million votes, though he lost.

Police said following his arrest that Quiboloy’s alleged victims were told they were having sex with the “spirit of God” and were threatened not to tell anyone on pain of being hunted down by “angels of death”.
Quiboloy’s church said at the time that members had “freedom of choice” and thus “anything that happens to you… is your own voluntary will or choice”. — AFP
1422e3c7730e1566: The Trump administration’s blind eye to severe human rights violations in Azerbaijan is deadly for political prisoners
Originally published on Global Voices
Bahruz Samadov being brought to Sabail District Court in 2024. Image by Voice of America, via Wikimedia Commons. Public domain.

Bahruz Samadov is an Azerbaijani political scientist, peace activist, and PhD candidate at Charles University in Prague, or at least he was until the summer of 2024. On August 21, 2024, the State Security Service detained Samadov while he was visiting his grandmother in Baku. Global Voices reported on his arrest at the time, as part of a wider crackdown on critics before Azerbaijan hosted COP29 in November 2024.

Samadov was one of the few Azerbaijani voices to oppose the 2020 Karabakh war. In his writing for OC Media, Eurasianet and other outlets, he argued for dialogue with Armenia and criticized the expulsion of ethnic Armenians from Karabakh. Prosecutors charged him with high treason based on his WhatsApp exchanges with Armenian peace activists and on publicly available information. Samadov denied the charges and called himself a “prisoner of peace.” His lawyer argued that the prosecution’s theory of “indirect espionage” was vague and had no basis in case law.

On June 23, 2025, after a closed-door trial, the Baku Grave Crimes Court sentenced him to 15 years in prison. The Baku Court of Appeal upheld the verdict in September 2025, and the Supreme Court did the same in September 2026. Amnesty International, which considers him arbitrarily imprisoned, reports that he has been held in solitary confinement and denied medical care, and that he has twice attempted suicide, most recently in his Supreme Court hearing. Below, Global Voices publishes a letter Samadov wrote from prison and asked us to share.

The 2024 summer holidays ended in a nightmare: while visiting Baku, my home city, from my doctoral studies in Prague, I was detained by the notorious State Security Service of Azerbaijan and soon was charged with “high treason.”

Studying the ideological tenets of the hegemonic regime in my homeland, I directly connected its durability to the conflict between Azerbaijan and Armenia, revealing the narratives of “national unity” under the “savior strongman.”

During and after the outbreak of the 2020 War in Karabakh, I criticized the deployment of military means. Between 2021–2024, I partook in various conferences and meetings across Europe, presenting my perspective and calling for a meaningful and inclusive policy of peace and co-existence.

The Azerbaijani regime, having years of the crackdown experience, is aggressively intolerant to any kinds of contestation, and especially targets the independent academic voices. When the repressive machinery was re-launched in late 2023, the regime started the total crackdown on civil society, independent media, politicians, and academicians.

In private communications, more than five political prisoners connected it to the worsened relations with the Biden administration. The latter was highly critical to the human rights violations in Azerbaijan.

Weeks before leaving the White House, Blinken invited human rights defender Rufat Safarov to Washington to receive the Human Rights Defender Award. Several hours after visiting the US Embassy in Baku, Safarov was arrested and accused of hooliganism and fraud. It was an open signal to the US that the leaving administration had no power to endorse the Azerbaijani critical voices.

The Azerbaijani government acted differently with the Trump administration. The August 8, 2025 meeting and the peace agreement was the soon-disappeared sign of hope for us. Even if the peace agreement did not include any references to human rights, the current administration’s plans for the long-term involvement in the region brought hopes for at least minimal reforms in Azerbaijan.

Curiously, my sham trial was “fastened” and ended on June 23, 2025 — a process too explicitly controversial to the “peace agenda.” Following the US delegation’s visit to Baku in January 2026, a number of political prisoners, me among them, appealed to the US officials to raise the “political prisoners issue” to the official Baku — a policy that once partially worked during Obama’s second term.

However, the recent severe sentences and USA’s silence prove our call remained rather a mere cry from the chamber cells. The Baku-based team of Toplum TV, the veteran human rights defender Anar Mammadli and others have received up to 15 years of imprisonment. To compare, the EU Parliament recently adopted a resolution calling for the release of political prisoners in Azerbaijan. Similar calls were made by the PACE and even the UN.

Meanwhile, the Trump administration is proud to end the violence in the South Caucasus (by the way, this narrative is implicitly contested by the official Baku — there D. Trump remains a mere “witness.”) While the Administration of White House endorses officials like Hikmet Hajiyev for their nice compliments to D. Trump and villanization of “Biden–Blinken couple,” the sufferings of Azerbaijani imprisoned dissent keep going.

Many of those fellow political prisoners I had a chance to talk to remain pessimistic and sceptical regarding the US involvement in the region, dismissing the possibility of the “Belarusian scenario.” One prominent political prisoner even rejected to sign the aforementioned call: “They came for security-related issues, they do not care about human rights,” he shouted from the cell’s balcony. “We are Biden’s prisoners,” laughed my inmate, an imprisoned journalist and poet.

True, nothing publicly known has been made by the Trump administration related to severe human rights violations in Azerbaijan. If the Republican administration aspires to replace Russia in the long-term in the South Caucasus, it should not abandon the ideals of the Founding Fathers in the foreign policy standards. Washington has officially repeatedly mentioned the human rights violations in rival countries like Iran, Cuba, and formerly Venezuela. The selective attitude to the human rights issues and turning the blind eye to our suffering endangers the democratic security of the US itself, not to mention its international image. This policy raises questions about the adherence to the American ideals of the current administration.

Yet, it is still not too late to follow the recommendations of Amnesty International: “Use every available opportunity, in bilateral and multilateral forces, to raise concerns about Azerbaijan’s human rights record.”
Bahruz Samadov Umbaku Prison 27.10.2026
Written by Global Voices Eurasia
526392856431b242: KUALA LUMPUR: The government will continue addressing issues affecting the Indian community, particularly in education and welfare, including the development of Tamil schools and promotion of the Tamil language.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the government recognised that more needed to be done to ensure the community's needs were addressed effectively.
"This also applies to issues involving Hindu temples, Indian traders and the lives of poor Indians in cities and estate areas.
"We must make an effort to address and resolve these issues," he said.
He was speaking at the national-level Deepavali celebration in Little India, Brickfields, today.

Also present were National Unity Minister Datuk Aaron Ago Dagang, his deputy R. Yuneswaran, Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan, Digital Minister Gobind Singh Deo, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil and Malaysian Associated Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry president Datuk Seri N. Gobalakrishnan.

Anwar said the Madani government would ensure welfare assistance was channelled according to people's needs, regardless of race, as part of efforts to ensure all segments of society benefited from the country's development.
"When we introduce programmes such as Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) and Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (Sara), we also take into account the needs of the people.
"In January, when schools reopen, our children in all schools, from all communities and in all districts, will receive assistance of RM200 per pupil.
"Why? Because we are thinking about their future."
On the Deepavali celebration, Anwar said Malaysians should embrace togetherness, mutual respect and appreciation despite their differences.
"We come here in a spirit of family, like old friends. Sometimes, we have not seen each other for a long time.
"Sometimes, we have never even met before. But, you know, we like each other and respect each other.
"We are different. Our skin colours, religions, cultures, mother tongues and ancestry are different.
"But we share common human values. We respect and appreciate one another. That is how Malaysia must be, must remain and must succeed as Malaysia," he said.
5a8ab5db485e5c5f: MELAKA, Nov 14 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) candidate for Pengkalan Batu Jason Tze-Xi Nathan says he committed no election violation when his voting was briefly halted at Sekolah Menengah Kebangsaan Agama Sultan Muhammad in Batu Berendam today.
He said the confusion arose because the presiding officer was unsure whether a candidate was allowed to vote.
Sinar Harian and Malaysia Gazette reported that the officer paused the process to seek clarification from his superiors after seeing a social media group message claiming candidates could not vote.
“The incident occurred when I arrived at the polling station at 9am and was receiving my ballot paper.
“The process resumed about two minutes later, once confirmation was received after the officer consulted his superiors,” Tze-Xi Nathan said.
He said he was eventually allowed to cast his vote.
He said he is a registered voter in Pengkalan Batu and had voted at the same polling station before.
He stressed that being a candidate did not strip him of his right to vote as a registered voter.
However, he did not fault the officer, saying the man might be new to the role.
“I don’t blame him, as he appeared quite young and it may well have been his first time serving as a presiding officer.
“Furthermore, seeking clarification from his superiors to resolve the situation was well within his authority,” he was quoted as saying.

Tze-Xi Nathan is in a four-way fight in Pengkalan Batu against Barisan Nasional (BN) candidate Siti Aisyah Mahmood, Parti Bersama Malaysia (Bersama) candidate Goh Han Koon and Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (Bersatu) candidate Datuk Norhizam Hassan Baktee.
There are 25,948 registered voters in Pengkalan Batu for this state election.
fffe3ee2ffb0d818: MELAKA: For newlyweds Nur Farah Ain Mustamam and Aidil Aimin Othman, their wedding day came with an added responsibility as they cast their ballots in the Melaka election.
Still dressed in their wedding attire, the couple, both 27, turned heads when they arrived at SK Jalan Datuk Palembang, a polling centre for the Bukit Katil state constituency, today.
The couple had tied the knot at 9am, just hours before heading to the polling centre, making their special day even more memorable.
Aidil, from Paya Ikan, said their solemnisation ceremony was initially scheduled for 10.30am but had been brought forward to ensure they had enough time to vote.
"It was a little hectic," he said when asked about juggling his wedding ceremony and his responsibility as a voter.
For Nur Farah, from Kampung Ku Sayang in Bukit Baru, the unusual circumstances made their wedding day all the more special.
"I'm happy because we get to go out and vote in our wedding attire. Everyone else is dressed normally, but here we are in our wedding clothes," she said with a laugh.
She admitted feeling slightly embarrassed by the attention they attracted, particularly from other voters who were surprised to see a bride and groom at the polling centre.
The couple had planned their wedding a year in advance, long before the polling date was announced.
Nur Farah said they had initially expected the state election to be held in early October and were caught off guard when Nov 14 was announced as polling day.
"We had already made all the bookings, including the wedding dais, so we decided to proceed with our original date," she said.
Despite their tight schedule, the couple were determined not to miss the opportunity to exercise their right to vote.
After accompanying her husband to SK Jalan Datuk Palembang, Nur Farah said they would head to another polling centre in Bukit Baru so she could cast her ballot.
Both said this was their third time voting.
Asked about their hopes for Melaka's future, the newlyweds said they wanted the next state government to govern responsibly and fulfil its election promises.
"We hope whoever forms the next state government will administer Melaka well and deliver on the promises made to the people," Nur Farah said.
0248418cc6a869c4: KUALA LUMPUR: Perdana Menteri Anwar Ibrahim menegaskan beliau mahu terus bertahan sebagai pemimpin yang mencintai negara, bukan mengikut desakan supaya dasar kerajaan berteraskan dominasi Melayu demi kelangsungan politik.
Beliau berkata demikian berikutan berdepan naratif daripada pihak tertentu yang mendakwa dasar negara perlu disesuaikan dengan dominasi Melayu, jika mahu terus bertahan dalam politik.
"Orang kata Anwar, kamu mesti menyesuaikan diri dengan dasar itu mesti berteraskan Melayu, dominasi Melayu. Jika tidak, kamu tidak akan dapat bertahan.

“Saya jawab, saya mahu terus bertahan sebagai pemimpin Malaysia yang mencintai negara ini," katanya ketika berucap dalam Majlis Sambutan Hari Deepavali Peringkat Kebangsaan 2026 di Little India, Brickfields.
Dalam pada itu, Anwar berkata beliau mahu mempertahankan prinsip negara dan Perlembagaan, termasuk kedudukan Bahasa Melayu, agama Islam serta hak dan keselamatan orang Melayu.
Beliau bagaimanapun mengingatkan keselamatan dan kestabilan negara turut bergantung kepada jaminan keadilan, kejayaan serta kebahagiaan untuk semua kaum dan setiap rakyat Malaysia.
Menurutnya, kekayaan negara perlu dimanfaatkan untuk memakmurkan seluruh rakyat tanpa mengira kaum kerana kemiskinan bukan hanya melibatkan satu kelompok masyarakat.
Beliau berkata, ada orang Melayu, Cina, India, Iban dan Kadazan yang berjaya, namun masih terdapat golongan miskin dalam setiap komuniti yang memerlukan perhatian kerajaan.

Sementara itu, Anwar mendakwa ada pihak menggunakan isu kaum untuk mengalihkan perhatian daripada isu rasuah dan penipuan, sedangkan sebahagian individu yang lantang bercakap mengenai kelangsungan kaum adalah antara yang terkaya di negara ini.
“Perjuangan itu sebenarnya untuk memperkayakan diri mereka dan keluarga mereka,” katanya.

Mengaitkan mesej Deepavali dengan perpaduan, Anwar berkata, Pesta Cahaya membawa simbol menghapuskan kegelapan serta memberi pencerahan kepada masyarakat untuk menjadi lebih adil, saksama dan bermoral.

Beliau turut mengakui masih terdapat beberapa perkara membabitkan masyarakat India yang perlu diperbaiki, termasuk pendidikan, sekolah Tamil, isu kuil Hindu, peniaga serta kemiskinan masyarakat itu di bandar dan ladang.

Katanya, kerajaan berusaha membantu semua kaum menerusi pelbagai inisiatif termasuk bantuan RM200 bagi setiap anak sekolah pada Januari, tanpa mengira kaum dan daerah, bagi meringankan beban keluarga menjelang pembukaan sekolah.
ac66e23fdb725e65: TEHRAN: Iran's navy and Revolutionary Guards said on Saturday that fires had broken out on a total of three oil tankers that struck mines in the Strait of Hormuz, where Tehran has restricted navigation.
Tehran has insisted that vessels obtain its authorisation to cross the strait since war erupted with the US in February, and has attacked ships that do not comply.

"A short while ago, two oil tankers that had switched off their radar and positioning systems and were secretly attempting to transit the Strait of Hormuz through an unauthorised route exploded and caught fire after striking a naval mine," the Guards' navy said in a statement on the incident in the south of the waterway, carried by the Iranian state broadcaster early on Saturday.

A separate statement from Iran's conventional navy said another tanker "navigating through the unsafe and prohibited zone east of the Strait of Hormuz with its tracking and identification systems switched off, caught fire and was forced to stop after striking a naval mine".
The statements did not provide the names or origins of the vessels but the Guards said one of those hit in south Hormuz was a supertanker.
The US has imposed a naval blockade on Iranian ports in response to Tehran's choking of the strategic trade route and provides military support to tankers using the waterway.
Iran's armed forces have reported several fires or explosions on board ships in the strait in recent weeks, often saying the vessels had struck mines.
The Guards released footage on Friday of a large plume of smoke rising from a vessel it said was carrying liquefied gas and hit a mine in the south of the strait.
However, the US military says it has cleared the main routes through the waterway of mines.

He could be British, she maintained, but “never be English”. Jean defended Englishness as though it were a possession she would never surrender to the country’s Black populace. Lammy’s entreaties to recognise it as a civic identity were ignored, as Jean attempted to demarcate its racial boundary live, on air. After cross-party condemnation of Jean’s nativist screed, Lammy would go on to appeal for census options that would allow him, his children and other Black people building lives in England to identify as English, but the Office for National Statistics (ONS) stood firm. c7bcd318382836cc: MANILA: A Philippine court has ordered the arrest of a jailed preacher sought by Washington for alleged child sex trafficking, a step toward his possible extradition to the United States, Manila said Saturday.

Self-proclaimed "Son of God" Apollo Quiboloy is currently being held without bail in a Philippine prison while on trial for a separate charge of human trafficking, which carries life in prison if convicted.
Manila filed a petition with a lower court on Monday to authorise his extradition to the United States, Philippine justice department spokesman Polo Martinez told AFP.

On Thursday, the court issued an extradition warrant of arrest against Quiboloy and two female associates – both at large – "after finding probable cause that each extraditee committed the offence or offences charged," Martinez added.
Under Philippine law, the court must now hold hearings before a final decision is made on the transfer.
Quiboloy, an ally of former president Rodrigo Duterte, was arrested in 2024 and later pleaded not guilty to the Philippine charges.
A US grand jury separately indicted Quiboloy in 2021 for conspiracy to engage in sex trafficking by force, fraud and coercion, sex trafficking of children and bulk cash smuggling.
The US indictment alleges women were recruited as personal assistants for Quiboloy, said to be in his mid-70s, to prepare his meals, clean his residence, give him massages and have sex with him.
Washington formally sought his extradition in August.

Martinez, the justice department spokesman, told AFP the Philippine court also issued a separate "hold departure order" against Quiboloy and his two associates to "prevent any attempt by each of them to depart from the Philippines."
Quiboloy's Kingdom of Christ sect claims millions of followers in the mainly Catholic Asian nation and owns a television network.
He was allowed to run for Senate in the country's 2025 midterm elections despite his incarceration and garnered 5.6 million votes, though he lost.

Police said following his arrest that Quiboloy's alleged victims were told they were having sex with the "spirit of God" and were threatened not to tell anyone on pain of being hunted down by "angels of death."
Quiboloy's church said at the time that members had "freedom of choice" and thus "anything that happens to you... is your own voluntary will or choice."--AFP
9aa2b1329522d6e8: KUALA LUMPUR: National doubles coaching director Rexy Mainaky hopes Toh Ee Wei can return to competition at next year's All England after her lengthy recovery from a knee injury.
However, he stressed that no comeback date has been fixed, with her condition and rehabilitation progress determining when she can reunite with mixed doubles partner Chen Tang Jie.
Ee Wei suffered an anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injury in her left knee during the Singapore Open quarter-finals in May.
She left for Melbourne in June to seek specialist treatment and underwent surgery later that month before continuing her rehabilitation in Australia.
Rexy confirmed that Ee Wei has returned to Malaysia and is expected to report to the Academy Badminton Malaysia (ABM) on Nov 20.
However, Rexy said she will need some rest before resuming training.
"We have to assess her condition first. She was in good hands in Australia, and we hope she will continue receiving the right support for her rehabilitation here," said Rexy.
"If everything goes well, we hope she can play at the All England. Otherwise, we hope she can return for the first tournament of the Olympic qualification campaign."
The qualifying period for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics will run from May 3, 2027 until April 30, 2028, with the Super 300 Taiwan Open on May 4 next year being the first tournament.
Rexy added that the priority was to ensure continuity in her rehabilitation after her return from Australia, while expressing hope that she would not remain out of competition for too long.

The knee injury forced Tang Jie-Ee Wei to miss their world title defence in New Delhi in August, with the BA of Malaysia (BAM) withdrawing the pair on medical advice to prioritise her long-term recovery.
Rexy also confirmed that Tang Jie-Ee Wei have ranking protection during her absence.
Their reunion will depend on Ee Wei's recovery, with the All England remaining a hoped-for comeback tournament rather than a confirmed return date.
e36070fc58c066db: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 14 — PAS President Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang has described the US Republicans and Democrats as two faces of the same dollar bill, while telling Muslims who are not yet in power that they may take sides without endorsing those they side with.
In a commentary dated today on the United States’ midterm elections, the Marang MP argued that the outcome of any American vote makes no difference to how Washington treats Islam.
“Although there are two big parties… the truth is that both are bound to the face of a one-dollar bill that carries two different pictures, yet its value remains the same one dollar,” Hadi wrote.
“Whichever party wins the election, their attitude towards Islam remains the same,” he said.
He claimed that both parties sit under the umbrella of “Zionist Jews” whose single struggle is to conquer the world under a Greater Israel as the sole superpower, without offering evidence.

Hadi also alleged that Freemasons and Zionists control the economy and media, and that the World Bank, the International Monetary Fund and financial institutions fund election machinery and media “free to lie and deceive”.
On how Muslims should respond, he said they are told not to give their allegiance to major powers and enemies of Islam, except where they are not yet in power.
“In such circumstances, Muslims are permitted to practise taqiyyah without giving their approval,” he said, referring to the concealment of one’s beliefs to protect oneself.

Citing Surah al-Rum and the Islamic principle of bearing the lesser of two harms, Hadi said siding temporarily with the less dangerous enemy is “not running away, but choosing to defeat the bigger enemy first, even though both are enemies of Islam”.
He added that while Muslims are allowed such concessions when weak, abandoning Islamic principles that must be defended with sacrifice and determination is forbidden.
Hadi said the light of Islam has now entered “the biggest and most ferocious colonial country” in the Muslim world’s history, and that Islamophobia has made many people curious about the religion.
“Let the enemy fall in its own internal fight,” he said.
He described Western democracy as one that “demeans religion and worships the dollar” and is “burning itself”, choosing “the foolish, wicked, deceitful or negligent” as national leaders.
Hadi urged Muslims to “take the opportunity” from the freedoms in Western democracy to declare Islam and practise it, and to fight for their rights to religion and worship.
“Never cross the limits set by Allah… never surrender and never act extremely,” he said.
Hadi also cited former US president Abraham Lincoln’s remark that “you can fool all the people some of the time, and some of the people all the time, but you cannot fool all the people all the time”.
He said the truth of Islam would be proven and that liars and deceivers would eventually be exposed.

Hadi has previously courted controversy by likening the confidence and supply agreement between Putrajaya and Opposition MPs to the deception of the Dajjal, the great deceiver whose emergence Islam regards as a sign that Judgement Day is near.
ef5209c0386401cd: MELAKA: A 22-year-old factory worker went straight to the polling station after completing his night shift to cast his ballot for the first time in the Melaka election today.
Despite having little time to rest, Muhammad Fakhrul Naim Umar joined his two younger siblings and their mother at SK Bertam Ulu about 10am.
He said he had finished work about 7am but did not want to miss the opportunity to fulfil his responsibility as a voter, especially as his two younger siblings were also voting.
Fakhrul said the experience was meaningful as he hoped the choices made by voters would contribute to a better economic situation in the future.
"My hope is that those entrusted with the mandate to serve as elected representatives will work to improve the current economic situation," he said when met at the polling centre today.
His younger brother, Muhammad Farish Nazhan, 18, said he had followed the candidates' campaigns and updates on social media, including TikTok, before deciding who to vote for.
He said he was also familiar with some candidates through the assistance they had provided to his family, including food aid when he was still a student.
"I will certainly choose those who have helped my family before, and I will reflect my appreciation for that assistance through my vote," he said.

Their sister, Bibi Farhana Najwa, 21, said she was excited about voting for the first time and that the family had chosen to go to the polling station in the morning to avoid crowds around noon and in the afternoon.
"I also work, so having the whole family come out to vote together makes the occasion lively. It is a new experience for the three of us who are voting for the first time," she said.
Meanwhile, first-time polling worker Muhd Aminuddin Mohd Shukri, 21, said he was serving as a polling clerk and usher at SK Bertam Ulu after applying for the role online in August.
The Masjid Tanah Community College student, who is pursuing a Certificate in Design Technology, said he had cast his ballot through a postal vote to enable him to carry out his duties on polling day.
A voter in the Sungai Udang state constituency, he said the experience gave him an opportunity to observe the voting process first-hand and interact with voters from various backgrounds.
Another polling worker, Muhammad Remmy Shah, 21, who works at a hotel and votes in the Pantai Kundor state constituency, took leave from work today to help ensure the voting process ran smoothly.
He said he also wanted to gain experience, adding that the atmosphere was something people did not get to experience every day, as elections were held only once every four to five years.
"Besides gaining experience, we also get to witness the spirit of unity when people of different races come out to vote and help one another, including by showing voters the way," he said.
3d52a52a3a982274: SEOUL: South Korea should neither fear China's rise nor underestimate its capabilities, Foreign Minister Cho Hyun said on Saturday, urging deeper cooperation ahead of a regional summit in China next week.

"During this visit to China, I was reminded that we should neither have an unfounded fear of China's rise nor underestimate its capabilities and potential," Cho wrote on X, saying Seoul should build cooperation benefiting both countries by drawing on the autonomy and creativity of its people and companies.
Cho's remarks came after talks and dinner with Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi in Beijing on Friday, their first meeting in about three months.
The ministers discussed bilateral ties, issues on the Korean Peninsula and ways to deliver tangible benefits to people in both countries

The meeting came ahead of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) leaders' summit in Shenzhen on Nov 18-19, which South Korean President Lee Jae Myung will attend. Lee is also scheduled to join a dinner hosted by Chinese President Xi Jinping and his wife, Seoul has said.

The summit is expected to bring together several major world leaders. US President Donald Trump is set to meet Xi and Russian President Vladimir Putin next Thursday on the sidelines of APEC, with nuclear arms reductions among the issues on the agenda, the White House said.
Cho said Seoul would seek to use Lee's visit to advance bilateral ties and expand "horizontal and mutually beneficial" cooperation in areas where the two countries have complementary strengths.

Lee's administration has sought to improve relations with China, South Korea's largest trading partner, after ties were strained under former president Yoon Suk Yeol, while maintaining Seoul's security alliance with the US.

Wang said on Friday that China wanted to expand cooperation with South Korea in traditional industries and emerging sectors including artificial intelligence and biomedicine. He said bilateral ties had returned to the right track after exchanges between the two countries' leaders.

Defence minister Khaled Nordin said two aircraft had been delivered so far, while another four were scheduled to arrive in April next year, ahead of the Langkawi International Maritime and Aerospace Exhibition (LIMA) 2027.

“All the aircraft will be based in Kuantan, Pahang, while their subsequent deployment will be considered after the Hawk aircraft are decommissioned,” he told reporters after the MADANI Adopted School handover ceremony at Sekolah Kebangsaan Panchor here today.
Malaysia signed a contract with Korea Aerospace Industries (KAI) in 2023 to procure 18 FA-50M aircraft for nearly RM4 billion under the 12th Malaysia Plan.

a4963254b414c3eb: AYER KEROH: A 20-member delegation of the Asian Women Parliamentarian Caucus (AWPC) was in Melaka today to witness the voting process for the state election.
Public Accounts Committee chairman Mas Ermieyati Samsudin said the visit was held in conjunction with the AWPC 2026 meeting taking place in Kuala Lumpur from Nov 12 until today.

"Since the state election is taking place today, I brought them down to Melaka to follow the democratic voting process and see how it works here," Mas Ermieyati, who is also a member of the AWPC, told FMT.
The delegation consisted of MPs from countries including the Philippines, Taiwan, South Korea, Japan, Nepal, Sri Lanka, Pakistan, India, Timor-Leste, and the Maldives.
It visited several polling locations in Melaka, including constituencies where women candidates are contesting, to observe the election atmosphere and operations.

Mas Ermieyati said the AWPC delegation also visited Parliament on Nov 12 and met Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim and opposition leader Hamzah Zainudin, and attended a luncheon with Senate president Awang Bemee Awang Ali Basah.

0e8a96e8bf9760a9: KOTA TINGGI: The Defence Ministry will receive another four FA-50M light combat aircraft next April, ahead of the Langkawi International Maritime and Aerospace Exhibition (Lima) 2027.
Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said the delivery would bring the number of FA-50M aircraft received by the Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) to six.
The aircraft are developed by South Korea's Korea Aerospace Industries (KAI).
He said the remaining 12 aircraft would be delivered in stages by March 2028, completing the delivery of all 18 aircraft procured by the government.
"We received two of the aircraft at the end of October. Before Lima, we will receive another four.

"After that, we will receive all 18 aircraft in stages by March 2028," he told reporters after officiating the launch of the Malaysia Defence Intelligence Organisation's (MDIO) Madani Adopted School programme at Sekolah Kebangsaan Panchor here today.
Khaled said all 18 light combat aircraft would be based in Kuantan, Pahang.
He said the possibility of deploying the aircraft to other locations would be considered after the RMAF retired its Hawk aircraft from service.

The aircraft arrived at the RMAF Labuan Air Base after being flown from Sacheon, South Korea.
Malaysia signed a contract with KAI in 2023 to procure 18 FA-50M aircraft worth nearly RM4 billion under the 12th Malaysia Plan.
The aircraft were acquired under the Fighter Lead-In Trainer-Light Combat Aircraft (FLIT-LCA) programme to replace the RMAF's ageing Hawk aircraft.
They will also serve as advanced training aircraft for fighter pilots and carry out light combat missions.

bad1e5cd9a8d06d1: SYDNEY: Australian captain Pat Cummins wants to draw a line under "Sandpapergate" and move on, but the stench of the 2018 ball-tampering scandal is set to linger after a week of sensational accusations and denials.

Cummins held an intense 70-minute press conference on Friday and answered every question thrown at him after former teammate Usman Khawaja reopened old wounds with the release of his explosive autobiography.
In the book, he claimed the whole team, including Cummins, knew about the plot to alter the ball with sandpaper during the Cape Town Test against South Africa.

Only David Warner, Steve Smith and Cameron Bancroft were held responsible by Cricket Australia for the incident that shattered the nation's reputation, with all three sent home in disgrace and banned.
Cummins repeated multiple times that he was not aware of the plan, insisting Khawaja's version of events was "100 percent wrong."
"I don't want to talk about this again after today ... because at some point we've got to move on," he added.
His plea drew support from Justin Langer, who took over as head coach when Darren Lehmann quit in the wake of the scandal.
"Hopefully, that will put some sort of line in the sand because we have to move on," Langer told SEN radio.
"There's too many people being hurt in Australian cricket ... and that includes the Australian public.

"When I talk about Australian cricket, it's about the public, it's about the fans, it's about the players, it's about everyone who's involved: the past players, the present players, future players. We have to draw a line in the sand somewhere."
Another former Test great Greg Chappell also urged an end to the in-fighting.
"We don't want to see Australian cricket eating itself and having a little spat within the family," he told reporters.
"Hopefully Pat's put a bit of a line under it and we can start getting on with the summer of cricket."
While calls to put the issue to bed mount, it could blow up again with several key players yet to comment, notably Smith and Bancroft, while Khawaja has media commitments to sell his book.
Warner has strongly backed close friend Khawaja's new version of events, making clear he will not rest "until the truth is out there."
He ratcheted up the pressure on Saturday, claiming Cricket Australia's investigation "stinks of a cover-up."
- PICK YOUR SIDE -
"The biggest error of the Cummins Q and A was his belief that his appearance would allow everyone to draw a line under the affair and move on," national broadcaster ABC said in an analysis.
"That's not happening. We're dealing with hurt feelings here, fractured relationships and bruised egos and nebulous concepts of truth and justice.
"You better pick your side, if you haven't already, because this is never going away."
Whether what really happened is ever properly established remains to be seen with Cricket Australia adamant it will not be re-opening its investigation.
But the bonds of a 15-year friendship between Cummins, Khawaja and Warner have splintered.
Cummins accused Khawaja of being "flippant and casual" by dropping his bombshell claims eight years after the fact, suggesting some of them were "probably defamatory."
That prompted Warner to blast Cummins for throwing Khawaja "under the bus" and The Australian newspaper to declare that "a generation of Australian players is officially at war."

Cummins insists unity within the current Australian team, which includes Smith, remains strong despite the week's firestorm as they prepare for a home Test series against New Zealand in December-January.
He said he had spoken to Smith, who lost the captaincy and was banned for a year over "Sandpapergate", and suggested the veteran batsman was keen not to regurgitate the past.
"I have spoken to Smithy. Without breaking confidence, he is done with this, he wants to move on," said Cummins.
"This was very traumatic for him. If standing up today and answering all your questions helps everyone move on, then maybe it's a good thing."--AFP

0095a06887318975: MELAKA: Kekurangan upaya fizikal bukan penghalang buat pasangan kembar wanita kerdil berusia 63 tahun untuk hadir menunaikan tanggungjawab sebagai pengundi pada PRN Melaka ke-16, hari ini.

1d535dfd6173f6e6: MASJID TANAH: Sebuah kenderaan membawa calon Pakatan Harapan (PH) bagi Tanjung Bidara, Yunazri Mustamiri diarah keluar dari kawasan pusat mengundi kerana memaparkan logo parti di zon larangan berkempen.

db9b419678ed2b15: MELAKA: Three generations of a family turned polling day into a special occasion, with four members casting their ballots together at Sekolah Jenis Kebangsaan Cina Notre Dame in the 16th Melaka election.

Leading the family was 84-year-old Lee Nyonya, who was accompanied by her son, Lim Man Hong, 65; daughter-in-law, Tan Lucy, 61; and granddaughter, Kelly Lim, 45, to vote in the Kota Laksamana state constituency.

More family members, including Lee's great-grandchildren, were expected to arrive at the polling centre later in the afternoon, following the voting time slots recommended by the Election Commission (EC).

Lee, a mother of seven with 18 grandchildren and 21 great-grandchildren, said she had never missed an election since she first became eligible to vote, setting an example of civic responsibility for the younger generations of her family.
"I've been voting since I was young and have never missed an election. I've voted so many times that I've lost count, but to me, it's simply my duty," she said.
Lee also revealed an unusual family naming tradition, with all six of her brothers bearing the name Lee Baba, while all six of her sisters were known as Lee Nyonya.
Asked how the family avoided confusion with so many siblings sharing the same names, Lim said his grandmother had her own way of addressing each of them.
Lee said the identical names often sparked laughter and playful teasing among family members, bringing back fond memories of their younger days.

Meanwhile, Kelly said that although some family members lived overseas or worked in other states, they still made an effort to uphold their longstanding voting tradition and do their part for Melaka's future.
"We remind each other to vote in our family WhatsApp group. Some of our relatives in Singapore voted by post, while others couldn't make it because they're working in other states," she said.
The Kota Laksamana state seat is seeing a three-cornered contest involving incumbent Low Chee Leong (PH-DAP), Melvin Chua Kew Wei (BN-MCA) and Ethan Lim Zhi Hao (Bersama).
600f50034ed888b7: HANG TUAH JAYA: A polling station chief at SMK Agama Sultan Muhammad in Batu Berendam here nearly barred Pakatan Harapan's Pengkalan Batu candidate, Jason Tze-Xi Nathan, from casting his ballot over a false viral Whatsapp message.
Nathan said he had arrived at the polling centre at about 9am and was being handed his ballot paper when the station chief stopped him.
"He was unsure if candidates were allowed to vote, because he saw a message in a WhatsApp group chat stating that candidates cannot vote.
"So he needed to confirm the matter with a superior," he told FMT, adding that he was eventually allowed to cast his ballot.
Nathan, a registered Pengkalan Batu voter, said he did not blame the station chief for the mixup, since he was young and possibly the first time serving in the role.
Nathan is in a four-cornered contest for the Pengkalan Batu seat against Barisan Nasional's Siti Aisyah Mahmood, Bersatu's Norhizam Hassan Baktee and Bersama's Goh Han Koon.
0086db6e907bd93d: TEHERAN: Iran's navy and Revolutionary Guards said on Saturday that fires had broken out on a total of three oil tankers that struck mines in the Strait of Hormuz, where Teheran has restricted navigation.
Teheran has insisted that vessels obtain its authorisation to cross the strait since war erupted with the United States in February, and has attacked ships that do not comply.

"A short while ago, two oil tankers that had switched off their radar and positioning systems and were secretly attempting to transit the Strait of Hormuz through an unauthorised route exploded and caught fire after striking a naval mine," the Guards' navy said in a statement on the incident in the south of the waterway, carried by the Iranian state broadcaster early on Saturday.

A separate statement from Iran's conventional navy said another tanker "navigating through the unsafe and prohibited zone east of the Strait of Hormuz with its tracking and identification systems switched off, caught fire and was forced to stop after striking a naval mine."
The statements did not provide the names or origins of the vessels but the Guards said one of those hit in south Hormuz was a supertanker.
The United States has imposed a naval blockade on Iranian ports in response to Teheran's choking of the strategic trade route and provides military support to tankers using the waterway.
Iran's armed forces have reported several fires or explosions on board ships in the strait in recent weeks, often saying the vessels had struck mines.
The Guards released footage on Friday of a large plume of smoke rising from a vessel it said was carrying liquefied gas and hit a mine in the south of the strait.
However, the US military says it has cleared the main routes through the waterway of mines.--AFP

55793d5e255886a8: KUALA LUMPUR: Umno, not DAP, is straining the unity government's cooperation agreement, DAP legal bureau chairman Ramkarpal Singh said today.
He said the unity government was formed to ensure stable governance and economic recovery, not to create political uncertainty for narrow party interests.
"If there is any talk of breaching trust or violating the terms of our political cooperation and the agreement, the record speaks for itself.
"It is Umno's actions, not DAP's, that have strained the consensus and tested the limits of the agreement," he said in a statement.
He said DAP had always been a reliable and disciplined partner in government and remained committed to honouring the terms of the agreement.
"We continue to support the Prime Minister's reform and economic agenda, but we will not hesitate to speak the truth when the integrity of the coalition is compromised."

Ramkarpal was responding to remarks by Umno Information Chief Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said concerning DAP National Chairman Gobind Singh Deo's comments on Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi and the current state of cooperation within the Unity Government.

"She cites the Cooperation Agreement of the Malaysia Unity Government. If there are differences of opinion among coalition partners, the appropriate response is dialogue and consultation, not public pressure or demands for resignation.
"Azalina's statement is indeed amusing. Perhaps she should remind herself of the purpose of the agreement."
Ramkarpal said three moves by Umno had undermined government stability.
These included aligning with the opposition in state elections, including in Johor, Negri Sembilan and Melaka, while remaining part of the federal administration alongside PH.
He also cited ongoing public criticism of Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim by Umno leaders, saying it was weakening confidence in the government.
The third move was suggesting the dissolution of parliament before the end of its term, creating unnecessary political uncertainty.
Ramkarpal said DAP remained a disciplined government partner committed to Anwar's reform and economic agenda.
However, he said the party would speak out whenever the coalition's integrity was compromised.
906831cafe7a18e5: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has criticised certain groups for exploiting racial issues to divert public attention from fraud and corruption.
He said these groups often invoked racial survival and interests while covering up wrongdoing involving fraud and corruption.
"There are certain associations or parties that merely rake up racial issues to cover up corruption.
"They talk about the survival and interests of races, but at the same time cover up issues of fraud and corruption.
"They raise racial issues, even though those who speak about the survival of the races are among the wealthiest people in our society.
"In reality, their struggle is about enriching themselves and their own families," he said.
He was speaking at the national-level Deepavali celebration in Little India, Brickfields, today.

Also present were National Unity Minister Datuk Aaron Ago Dagang, his deputy R. Yuneswaran, Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan, Digital Minister Gobind Singh Deo, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil and Malaysian Associated Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry president Datuk Seri N. Gobalakrishnan.
Anwar also said that he would not bow to pressure from certain quarters seeking to change national policies in favour of racial dominance for political survival.
He reaffirmed his commitment to upholding the Federal Constitution and ensuring justice for all Malaysians.
"The government today, despite facing pressure to change national policies, continues to uphold the fundamental principles of our country."
Anwar said some quarters were calling on him to adjust national policies in favour of the Malays.
"They said: 'Anwar, you must adjust. The policy must favour the Malays and Malay dominance. Otherwise, you will not survive.'
"I replied: 'I want to survive as a Malaysian leader who loves this country.
I want to uphold our country's principles and our Constitution. No one should question the position of the Malay language, Islam and the special position of the Malays.
But we must remember that to ensure this country remains safe, we must guarantee justice, success and happiness for all races and every citizen.'"
Anwar said Malaysia was blessed with abundant wealth and resources, which should be used to ensure prosperity for all Malaysians, regardless of race or background.
"This country has strength. It possesses abundant wealth and resources. It should ensure prosperity for every one of its citizens," he said.
He said successful and poor people could be found across all ethnic communities.
"Our responsibility as a nation is to empower all our people and enhance the capabilities of every citizen," he said, adding that Malaysia could also learn from the experiences of other countries.

cd0e0974319271ac: KOTA TINGGI: Any decision on the strained relationship between Umno and DAP, including whether to dissolve Parliament, is up to Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
Umno vice-president Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said the prime minister had the authority to decide on the next course of action following differences between parties in the unity government.
"Ultimately, everything is up to the prime minister. He can dissolve Parliament, sack someone, suspend someone or do whatever he wants.
"If he remains silent, then everyone should remain silent. Why make all the noise? He is keeping quiet, while everyone else is making a fuss," he said.
He was commenting on four options proposed by Umno to address its strained ties with DAP, including the possibility of dissolving Parliament.

Umno information chief Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said yesterday outlined three other options: appointing a mediator through a consultative council, maintaining the existing arrangement or reviewing Paragraph C of the Coalition Agreement.
On the changing political landscape, Khaled said parties should accept that political arrangements could become more complex in the future.
He said it could become increasingly common for parties to cooperate at the federal level while adopting different political approaches at state level.
"We have entered a political landscape where we must accept that this may become the norm.

"The federal government may differ from state governments. A party may be part of the federal government but may not accept the participation of other parties forming the federal administration at state level," he said.
He also said cooperation between Umno and Pas should not be viewed as excluding other races or political parties.
He said cooperation among Malays was positive and did not prevent the participation of other parties.
"Cooperation between Umno and Pas does not reject other races. If they want to join, they can. Many have joined, including MCA, MIC and Gerakan.
"So how can Umno and Pas be accused of rejecting cooperation or refusing to accept other races?" he said.
Tensions between Umno and DAP have emerged following differences over the issue of a conditional pardon for former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak.

5a84fc6101742c6f: MELAKA, Nov 14 — A three-way contest featuring a former aide to the Melaka chief minister, a silat instructor and a former university information technology chief could be adding to the excitement in Serkam, which recorded the highest voter turnout among the state’s 28 constituencies today.

The Election Commission’s (EC) real-time Voter Turnout Monitoring dashboard showed that over 51 per cent of registered voters in N. 26 Serkam had cast their ballots as of 1pm, especially when contrasted against N. 22 Bandar Hilir’s 38.5 per cent.
The constituency had been leading the turnout the whole morning and the numbers are climbing fast.

The keen interest in Serkam comes amid a closely watched three-cornered contest between Barisan Nasional’s (BN) Datuk Azman Abdullah, Pakatan Harapan’s (PH) Muhammad Faiq Azman and Parti Bersama Malaysia’s (Bersama) Muhamad Saffie Md Yasan.
All three are first-time candidates, but bring markedly different backgrounds and approaches to the race.
Azman, 54, is BN’s new face in the constituency but is no stranger to local politics, having spent more than a decade working alongside elected representatives and serving residents.
The Kampung Tedong native was a special officer to the Melaka chief minister from 2024 to 2026, and previously served as Tedong Umno chief and deputy Jasin Umno chief.
He has said his experience working with elected representatives had given him an understanding of residents’ needs and the problems they face.
His challengers offer different profiles, with Faiq, 36, bringing his experience as a silat instructor and involvement in community associations.
The Bukit Katil Giatmara alumnus has been teaching silat with Persatuan Seni Silat Langkah Bromo since 2000 and is also a committee member of Persatuan Seni Silat Gerak Tepat.
Saffie, 53, meanwhile, brings 18 years of public-sector experience, including serving as chief information technology officer at Universiti Malaysia Kelantan (UMK) from 2007 to 2018.

The Bersama candidate holds a master’s degree in Information Technology in Manufacturing from Universiti Teknologi Malaysia and was involved in the planning committee for the establishment of UMK in 2006.

Although he is not originally from Serkam, Saffie has pledged to relocate to the constituency if elected, and has proposed using technology to improve public services, including a dedicated constituency application for complaints and welfare assistance.

The contest is particularly significant given Serkam’s narrow result in the 2021 Melaka election, when BN’s Datuk Zaidi Attan retained the seat with a majority of just 79 votes against Perikatan Nasional’s candidate.
Zaidi is not defending the seat this time, leaving BN to rely on Azman to retain the constituency against two challengers seeking to break its hold.
The close previous result, the change of BN candidate and the contrasting profiles of the three contenders make Serkam one of the constituencies worth watching as polling continues.
The EC is targeting a 70 per cent turnout in the Melaka election, which sees 79 candidates contesting 28 seats.
A total of 240 polling centres, comprising 1,213 polling streams, opened at 8am today and will close at 6pm.

PH is fielding the most candidates, contesting 24 seats, followed by BN with 23, Bersama with 16, Bersatu with seven, Perikatan Nasional (PN) with five, Parti Pribumi Perkasa Malaysia with one and three independents.
The election follows the dissolution of the 15th Melaka State Legislative Assembly on September 23, with the consent of Yang di-Pertua Negeri Tun Mohd Ali Rustam.
In the previous state election on November 20, 2021, BN won 21 of the 28 seats, while PH took five and PN secured two.
e6d52b1d9d176355: MELAKA, Nov 14 — The Election Commission (EC) expects the first result of the 16th Melaka State Election to be known by 9.30pm tonight, said EC chairman Datuk Seri Ramlan Harun.
He said the official results for all 28 State Legislative Assembly seats are expected to be known before midnight.

“We should be able to report the first result to the public by 9.30pm, and we anticipate that all results will be available before midnight,” he told reporters after visiting a polling station at SJK© Malim here today.
Commenting on the voter turnout, Ramlan noted that as of 11.25am, the turnout was quite encouraging at 31.07 per cent.
He expressed confidence that the minimum target of a 70 per cent voter turnout for this election could be achieved.

“I remain confident in the 70 to 75 per cent figure. A minimum of 70 per cent is achievable this time,” he said, while urging the public to come out and vote early, given the forecast of rain in the afternoon.
In a related development, Ramlan mentioned that over 7,000 registered voters with disabilities (OKU) have already cast their ballots.
Regarding voter turnout by gender, Ramlan said the turnout among female voters is currently higher than that of male voters, based on real-time data obtained through the EC’s OCR-VA system.
Commenting on election-related offences, Ramlan said 301 minor election offences had been reported as of last night, most of which involved the installation of campaign materials.
“I cannot say that 301 is a low figure. We hope that such incidents can be further reduced in the future,” he said.
He also expressed his appreciation to members of the public who came forward to report election offences, adding that the Election Commission (EC) has taken action regarding the complaints received.
According to data from the Election Commission (EC), 675,166 voters are eligible to cast their ballots today to elect representatives for 28 State Legislative Assembly seats. — Bernama
