25fe5f2c59d82da0: MANILA: A Philippine court has ordered the arrest of a jailed preacher sought by Washington for alleged child sex trafficking, a step toward his possible extradition to the US, Manila said Saturday.

Self-proclaimed "Son of God" Apollo Quiboloy is currently being held without bail in a Philippine prison while on trial for a separate charge of human trafficking, which carries life in prison if convicted.
Manila filed a petition with a lower court on Monday to authorise his extradition to the US, Philippine justice department spokesman Polo Martinez told AFP.

On Thursday, the court issued an extradition warrant of arrest against Quiboloy and two female associates -- both at large -- "after finding probable cause that each extraditee committed the offence or offences charged," Martinez added.
Under Philippine law, the court must now hold hearings before a final decision is made on the transfer.
Quiboloy, an ally of former president Rodrigo Duterte, was arrested in 2024 and later pleaded not guilty to the Philippine charges.
A US grand jury separately indicted Quiboloy in 2021 for conspiracy to engage in sex trafficking by force, fraud and coercion, sex trafficking of children and bulk cash smuggling.
The US indictment alleges women were recruited as personal assistants for Quiboloy, said to be in his mid-70s, to prepare his meals, clean his residence, give him massages and have sex with him.
Washington formally sought his extradition in August.

Martinez, the justice department spokesman, told AFP the Philippine court also issued a separate "hold departure order" against Quiboloy and his two associates to "prevent any attempt by each of them to depart from the Philippines".
Quiboloy's Kingdom of Christ sect claims millions of followers in the mainly Catholic Asian nation and owns a television network.
He was allowed to run for Senate in the country's 2025 midterm elections despite his incarceration and garnered 5.6 million votes, though he lost.

Police said following his arrest that Quiboloy's alleged victims were told they were having sex with the "spirit of God" and were threatened not to tell anyone on pain of being hunted down by "angels of death".
Quiboloy's church said at the time that members had "freedom of choice" and thus "anything that happens to you... is your own voluntary will or choice".
220a06293fa23127: MELAKA: Voters in Kesidang turned out in large numbers from 8am today, heeding calls by election authorities and party leaders to cast their ballots early to avoid midday traffic congestion and forecast afternoon thunderstorms.
The Election Commission (EC) and caretaker Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh had earlier encouraged Melakans to make the most of the fine morning weather.
This followed Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) forecasts of thunderstorms across the state later today.
The call was heeded at SJK (C) Malim, which serves the Taman Asean polling district under the Kota Melaka parliamentary constituency.
The polling district has 8,017 registered voters across 13 voting streams (saluran).
Many residents arrived well ahead of their assigned afternoon voting slots.
Among them was 38-year-old civil servant Ina Sazali, who decided not to wait until later in the day.
"My turn was actually in the afternoon, but because I was worried about traffic jams, I came out early.
"Thank goodness, there wasn't much of a crowd upstairs," she said, adding that she planned to drive her younger sibling to another polling centre.
Despite the election being held at state level, Ina said casting her ballot was important.
"We want to choose the best," she said.
Meanwhile, 67-year-old retiree Baba Pari also opted to vote early to avoid afternoon traffic congestion and possible rain.
Born and raised in Melaka, Baba said he had never missed an opportunity to vote, describing it as a duty every citizen must fulfil.
"Voting in an election is our responsibility as Malaysians. It allows us to determine who we should choose to maintain peace and security for everyone," he said.
He said it was encouraging to see younger voters joining older residents in casting their ballots today.
"My hope is that young people now understand that voting is a responsibility.
"It determines their own future, as well as that of generations to come," he said.
In the 16th Melaka state election, Kesidang is the state's largest constituency, with 54,910 registered voters.
Two-term incumbent Allex Seah Shoo Chin of PH is defending the seat in a three-cornered contest against Perikatan Nasional's Albert Kok Boon Chang and Bersama candidate Dr Bryan Kek Kit Hun.

6df70bb8ab3fea14: SEREMBAN: Negri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim has withdrawn his earlier objection to Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir's position as the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negri Sembilan, reaffirming his support for the ruler.
It is learnt that Ismail met the Keeper of the Rulers' Seal, Tan Sri Syed Danial Syed Ahmad, earlier this week and submitted a letter withdrawing his previous objection.

A letter dated Nov 10, sighted by Berita Harian, stated that Ismail had withdrawn the contents of his Sept 17 letter, taking into account the Malay Rulers' media statement dated Oct 14 and a June 5 Seremban High Court order which maintained Tuanku Muhriz's position as the Yang di-Pertuan Besar.

The letter said the decision was made in accordance with the Negri Sembilan Constitution 1959, to uphold the institution of the monarchy and ensure the state's administration continued peacefully and in an orderly manner.
It also stated that Ismail was expected to have an audience with Tuanku Muhriz to pledge his allegiance and seek the ruler's consent for the State Legislative Assembly (DUN) to reconvene.
The DUN sitting, originally scheduled to begin in mid-October, was cancelled and later rescheduled for Nov 26.
Ismail had previously said the crisis in Negri Sembilan, particularly the dispute involving the palace, would be resolved soon.
He said the matter had been discussed at both state and national Umno leadership levels, but declined to provide further details.
Deputy Prime Minister and Barisan Nasional chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi had also expressed confidence that the crisis would be resolved soon.
He said he hoped a solution could be reached through a spirit of cooperation among the parties involved, as had been demonstrated during the formation of the state government.

41a4aecef6ada6b3: LOS ANGELES: The injury-hit Indiana Pacers held off the New York Knicks 106-104 on Friday, thwarting a Knicks comeback bid to leave New York's bid for an NBA Cup repeat in tatters.
The Knicks won the 2025-26 in-season tournament in what proved a curtain-raiser to their run to a first NBA championship since 1973.
But after coming up short in their bid to erase a 14-point third-quarter deficit, the Knicks fell to 0-2 in Cup play.
They are not mathematically eliminated, but in three prior editions of the Cup, no team with two group stage defeats has reached the knockout rounds.

With Tyrese Haliburton still sidelined with a hamstring strain, Pascal Siakam scored 19 points to lead a balanced Pacers attack. Aaron Nesmith scored 18 points, Kelly Oubre Jr. added 16 and Ivica Zubac and Andrew Nembhard chipped in 12 apiece.
Jalen Brunson scored 33 points and handed out 11 assists for the Knicks, who tied it at 87-87 early in the fourth quarter only for the Pacers to pull away again with a 15-2 scoring run.

The Knicks made one last push, cutting the deficit to two, but Karl-Anthony Towns – who scored 23 points and pulled down 15 rebounds – missed a potential game-tying basket with nine-tenths of a second remaining.
"Very proud of our team. We were pretty big underdogs coming into this game," said Pacers coach Rick Carlisle, whose team out-scored the Knicks 50-30 in the paint.
"Second half, it got difficult. New York is a championship team. They know how to make comebacks," Carlisle said. "Our guys stuck together and kept fighting together."
The Knicks are last in East Group B and will host the Cleveland Cavaliers and Miami Heat in their last two Cup group games.
In Miami, Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo scored 37 points each to lead the Heat to a 133-121 victory over the Cleveland Cavaliers.
After dropping the first four games of the season, the Heat are seeing what they'd hoped for when they brought in Antetokounmpo to team with Adebayo.
Adebayo added 14 rebounds, and Davion Mitchell chipped in 22 points and 17 assists to help the Heat improve to 2-0 in Cup play – top of the group – and 6-6 on the season.
Donovan Mitchell led Cleveland with 25 points and James Harden added 20 but the Cavs have dropped three of their last four games.
Franz Wagner continued his stellar play for Orlando, scoring 35 points with nine rebounds and 12 assists to lead the Magic to a 107-99 victory over the Milwaukee Bucks.
The Magic earned their first home win of the season. Just 5-7 overall they improved to 2-0 in Cup play. - AFP

da8e54bdb82677c2: MELAKA, Nov 14 — More than 40 per cent of registered voters in Melaka had cast their ballots by noon today in the state election.

db34d86701724533: WASHINGTON: The US Federal Aviation Administration lifted a nationwide ground stop on Friday after a communications failure at air traffic control centers caused chaos at airports and triggered the longest nationwide shutdown since the Sept 11, 2001, attacks.

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said US airspace reopened at 8:15 p.m. Eastern Time (0115 GMT), but warned that departures would resume gradually and it would take time for airlines to restore normal operations.
"It's going to be slow," Duffy told reporters at the White House.

More than 6,600 flights were canceled and 8,600 delayed, with another 1,500 already cancelled for Sunday, according to FlightRadar24. Aviation analysts said the four-hour nationwide grounding could disrupt airline schedules for days.

Duffy said tens of thousands of passengers were stranded at airports around the country. Duffy said he and Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin had met with President Donald Trump in the Oval Office to discuss the outage.

The failure is the latest and most dramatic sign of strain on a US air traffic control system beset by aging technology, equipment and communications problems and a shortage of several thousand controllers.
Duffy said the trouble began at 3:36 pm, when air traffic control centers experienced instability in radar and communications systems.

"Our switches, our routers actually got overloaded with data and they started to give us inconsistencies in the data from those routers and because of that we shut the system down," Duffy said, adding that at no stage did they completely lose radar or communications and they were able to safely land thousands of planes.
Duffy said the immediate problem had been fixed and that flying was safe, but warned that a broader overhaul of the aging air traffic control system was needed to prevent similar failures.
US$50 billion aviation overhaul
Duffy blamed Congress for failing to fund a new system that he said could prevent such outages, and called for US$50 billion to modernize it.

Earlier on Friday, before the outage, the White House and Department of Transportation had urged Congress to approve US$30.1 billion to upgrade the nation's aging airports and air traffic control infrastructure.
"What we have is an incredibly old air traffic control system," Duffy said.
"Give us the money to fix it."
Homeland Security Secretary Mullin said there was "zero evidence" so far that the outage resulted from a cyberattack or a rogue AI system, though investigators had not ruled out either possibility.
"It appears this was mechanically driven, however, we're still looking," Mullin said.
The National Security Agency was working with the Department of Homeland Security on the investigation, he added.

The outage appeared to be affecting a telecommunications network overseen by L3Harris Technologies, according to two airline officials. The network handles critical radio frequencies used by air traffic controllers to communicate with pilots. L3Harris did not respond to a request for comment.
Pain not over for passengers

Though the ground stop was lifted, the disruption for passengers was far from over. From Boston to Seattle and New York to Los Angeles, passengers crowded departure halls and airline desks as delays and cancellations mounted and aircraft remained parked at gates.

Thousands of passengers faced being stranded overnight. Edward Kargbo, 50, from West Chester, Pennsylvania, had been scheduled to take a 9 p.m. Ethiopian Airlines flight to Lomé, Togo. Instead, he planned to spend the night at the airport before a rescheduled flight at 6 a.m. on Saturday.
“I have to squat the night here,” he said. “I’m stranded.”
Louise Maher, 47, was also caught up in the disruption at Newark after her British Airways flight to London was caught up in the aviation meltdown.
“I might cry at some point but not yet,” she said.
US airlines will not be required to provide compensation to stranded passengers because the carriers were not responsible for the FAA system failures.
The only other nationwide ground stop since the Sept 11 attacks came in January 2023, when the FAA halted domestic departures for about 90 minutes.

Investors were already pricing in a financial hit to airlines. Shares of American Airlines, United Airlines and Delta Air Lines fell between 1% and 2% in after-hours trading, while JetBlue Airways dropped about 3%.
American Airlines said it was prioritizing flights to smaller cities outside its major hubs and international destinations to position aircraft and crews for a faster recovery.

524dedd1ea828100: NOVEMBER 14 — On October 24, 2026, I returned to the Faculty of Engineering, Universiti Malaya, to celebrate the Silver Jubilee of its Department of Biomedical Engineering.

It was a memorable occasion, bringing together former and current lecturers, alumni, students and colleagues from the industry. For someone who had been involved in the early development of biomedical engineering at the university, the gathering brought back many memories of a time when the future of this relatively new discipline was far from certain.

One of the highlights was listening to Professor Wan Abu Bakar, the founding Chair of the Department, recount how it all began. His recollections reminded me of something that may surprise those who know biomedical engineering today as an established academic discipline.
Before there was a Department of Biomedical Engineering at Universiti Malaya, there were already students studying for a degree in the field.
The Bachelor of Biomedical Engineering programme had begun as an academic programme within the Faculty of Engineering, before it acquired the status of a full-fledged department in 2001.

That same year, its first cohort of students graduated. Among them was Nahrizul Adib Kadri, now a professor in the same department, who received the Anugerah Pelajaran Diraja, the university’s highest honour for graduating students.
It was an encouraging achievement for a programme that was still finding its place within the university and the wider professional community.
Looking back, I find something rather remarkable about those early years. We were preparing young people for careers in a discipline whose future in Malaysia had yet to be clearly established.
Unlike conventional engineering fields, biomedical engineering was still unfamiliar to many employers, prospective students and even fellow academics.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
The writer (seated fifth from right, second row) with alumni and founders of Universiti Malaya’s Department of Biomedical Engineering. — Picture courtesy of Ng Kwan Hoong

Its professional identity was developing, and the opportunities awaiting its graduates were not always obvious. Yet students enrolled, lecturers committed themselves to teaching, and the programme continued to grow.
Those involved in its development had many practical challenges to overcome. Bringing engineering and medicine together required more than combining subjects from two faculties.
We had to develop an appropriate curriculum, establish laboratories, acquire equipment and create meaningful connections with clinicians and hospitals.
As someone representing the medical faculty, I was particularly involved in strengthening the biomedical and clinical dimensions of the programme.
My own experience in medical physics had taught me that collaboration between different disciplines required patience, mutual understanding and a willingness to learn from one another.

There were also questions that nobody could answer with certainty. Would employers recognise the qualifications of our graduates? Would hospitals and healthcare institutions see the value of biomedical engineers? Could the programme attract enough students and academic staff to sustain itself over the years?

Twenty-five years later, the answers to many of those early questions were standing before us at the Silver Jubilee celebration. I was delighted to meet members of the pioneering student cohorts, although I must confess that I initially struggled to recognise some of them after so many years.
We exchanged stories about their university days, recalled familiar lecturers and laughed about experiences that had somehow survived the passage of time.

Their journeys had taken them in different directions. Some had become professors and researchers, while others had established careers in hospitals, industry, government agencies and regulatory bodies.

Their achievements were not identical, nor should they have been. What mattered was that a field once regarded as unfamiliar had opened doors to careers and contributions that were difficult to imagine when the programme first began.

Over the years, I have continued to enjoy teaching in the department, particularly Medical Imaging and Perspectives in Healthcare Technology. The latter has evolved considerably as healthcare technology has advanced, with greater attention to clinical engineering and the practical challenges of applying technology in healthcare settings.

The biomedical engineering of today encompasses developments in medical imaging, rehabilitation, medical devices, regenerative medicine, artificial intelligence and digital health that were still emerging, or scarcely imaginable, during the programme’s early years.

The Silver Jubilee gathering, thoughtfully organised under the leadership of the current Head of Department, Associate Professor Dr Juliana Usman, offered an opportunity to appreciate the many people who have contributed to this journey.
Dr Juliana herself belonged to that pioneering student cohort, a particularly meaningful reminder of how far the programme has come.

The founders provided the initial vision, successive generations of lecturers sustained and expanded the programme, and the students carried its influence into workplaces and institutions far beyond Universiti Malaya.
Anniversaries naturally encourage us to celebrate achievements. They also have a curious way of making the past appear more orderly than it actually was.
Looking back from the comfort of 25 years, it is easy to imagine that the department’s development followed a carefully laid plan, with each milestone leading inevitably to the next.
Those of us who remember the early years know that the journey involved uncertainty, difficult decisions and considerable faith in possibilities that had not yet been demonstrated.

Perhaps this is what I will remember most about the celebration. Before the department had its present identity, before its graduates had established their careers, and before biomedical engineering became a familiar part of Malaysia’s higher education landscape, there were people willing to begin.
There were academics who believed the discipline deserved a place in the university, and there were young students willing to invest their futures in something whose promise was still unfolding.
Looking at the people gathered for the Silver Jubilee, I felt grateful to have played a small part in that beginning, and even more grateful to see how much they had made of it.

* Ng Kwan Hoong is an emeritus professor of Biomedical Imaging at the Faculty of Medicine, Universiti Malaya. A 2020 Merdeka Award recipient, he is a medical physicist by training but also enjoys writing, drawing, listening to classical music and bridging the gap between older and younger generations. He may be reached at ngkh@ummc.edu.my.
** This is the personal opinion of the writer or publication and does not necessarily represent the views of Malay Mail.

531916d249e30962: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 14 — The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) will expand its internet user experience data collection initiative nationwide to identify areas requiring improvements in service quality, including locations not previously covered by existing test mapping.

MCMC chief officer of state affairs Bukhari Yahya said the Selangor Speed Test Month 2026 initiative, which ran from Sept 16 to Oct 15, had successfully identified areas with unsatisfactory internet service quality based on actual user tests.

“The findings would be analysed and used as a basis for discussions with service providers to ensure immediate remedial action was taken in the affected locations,” he said this when appearing as a guest on Radio Televisyen Malaysia’s (RTM) Selamat Pagi Malaysia programme titled ‘Bulan Speed Test Selangor 2026: Dari Data Kepada Tindakan’ on Friday.

Bukhari said tests conducted by users also helped MCMC identify discrepancies between coverage shown in computer-based analyses and actual experiences on the ground, which could be attributed to geographical factors and physical obstructions such as dense tree cover.
He said that although an area might have internet coverage, the service speed received by users might not meet the Mandatory Standard for Quality of Service (MSQoS) set by MCMC.

In this regard, public participation through the MCMC Nexus application, developed by the commission and launched last March, is crucial as it complements existing monitoring efforts carried out by MCMC officers at locations such as major economic and industrial areas.

“For example, doctors who use the internet in hospitals, teachers conducting PdPR (home-based teaching and learning) or traders, as many people no longer carry cash to make purchases or conduct business but instead use QR codes for payments,” he said.

Bukhari said the test data collected was anonymous, with MCMC only recording test results without capturing users’ personal information, adding that the public need not be concerned about using the application.

He said the initiative had the potential to be expanded nationwide, with subsequent implementation locations to be selected based on factors such as challenging terrain or states with high-impact economic areas.

He added that the data would also help MCMC assess internet coverage requirements at polling centres ahead of the next general election (GE), newly developed tourist destinations and along roads, in line with the ‘Di Mana Ada Jalan Di situ Ada Internet’ (Where There is a Road, There is internet) initiative launched by Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil.

Meanwhile, Selangor MCMC director Amal Abdul Aziz, who was also a guest on the programme, said the initiative recorded nearly 100,000 internet speed tests throughout its month-long implementation in the state.
He said nearly 30,000 contest entries were recorded, involving 1,746 participants, with each participant conducting an average of 17 tests during the period.

Selangor was chosen as the first location due to its large population and high number of internet users, as well as its diverse usage environments, including educational institutions, residential areas and industrial sectors.
Amal said engagement sessions with government agencies, penghulu, and village heads were also held to encourage participation among residents in villages and rural areas.

3c3d7b0f7b7d0468: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 14 — Justifying the oppression perpetrated by a particular leadership based on religious sentiments is a dangerous generalisation that places identity above the principles of justice and integrity.
Parti Keadilan Rakyat (PKR) Wanita chief Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek said Islamic teachings had never granted any ruler moral immunity.
Instead, she said the Islamic principle of al-adl (justice) required that everyone be treated justly, regardless of their religious or racial background or position.
“Corruption and abuse of power remain forms of oppression that must be opposed.
“Regrettably, religious sentiments continue to be exploited in politics to the extent of undermining trust among people of different faiths,” she said in a Facebook post.

c04c8712f119dcd2: PETALING JAYA: Seramai 252,109 atau 37.67%, pengundi telah menunaikan tanggungjawab mereka pada PRN Melaka setakat 12 tengah hari ini, menurut Suruhanjaya Pilihan Raya (SPR).
Jumlah itu lebih tinggi berbanding peratusan keluar mengundi sebanyak 36% yang direkodkan pada waktu sama dalam PRN sebelum ini pada November 2021.
SPR berkata Serkam mencatatkan peratusan keluar mengundi tertinggi iaitu 42.67%, diikuti Tanjong Bidara (42.23%) dan Ayer Molek (42.07%).
Peratusan keluar mengundi terendah pula direkodkan di Bandar Hilir (32.49%), Kesidang (33%) dan Sungai Udang (34.44%).
Peratusan keseluruhan keluar mengundi dalam PRN 2021 ialah 65.85%.
Semua pusat mengundi di 28 kawasan DUN dijadualkan ditutup pada 5 petang.
Seramai 669,211 pengundi layak menunaikan tanggungjawab mereka dalam pilihan raya ini, yang diadakan susulan pembubaran DUN pada 23 Sept.

Kerajaan negeri sebelum ini dibentuk oleh Barisan Nasional (BN) selepas pilihan raya 2021, dengan gabungan itu menguasai 21 daripada 28 kerusi apabila Sulaiman Ali memperoleh penggal kedua sebagai ketua menteri.

Bagaimanapun, perebutan kuasa dalaman menyebabkan Sulaiman meletakkan jawatan dan Ketua Umno Melaka, Ab Rauf Yusoh, mengambil alih jawatan tertinggi itu serta membawa Pakatan Harapan (PH) menyertai pentadbirannya pada April 2023.

Pada Julai, PH menarik diri daripada semua jawatan dalam kerajaan negeri susulan ketegangan yang semakin meningkat dengan BN, selain membantah kelulusan pindaan perlembagaan yang membenarkan pelantikan sehingga tujuh Adun yang tidak dipilih melalui pilihan raya.
Dalam pilihan PRN ini, BN bertanding di 23 daripada 28 kerusi yang dipertandingkan menerusi pakatan dengan Perikatan Nasional, yang bertanding lima kerusi.
PH pula bertanding di 24 kerusi dengan kerjasama Bersatu, yang meletakkan tujuh calon.
ebf0ba6309509662: PETALING JAYA: Presiden PAS Hadi Awang berkata umat Islam dibenarkan berpihak sementara kepada pihak yang dianggap kurang berbahaya bagi menghadapi musuh lebih besar, ketika berada dalam keadaan lemah dan tidak berkuasa.
Beliau berkata pendekatan itu berlandaskan prinsip memilih mudarat lebih ringan antara dua kemudaratan, tanpa mengorbankan prinsip Islam yang wajib dipertahankan.

“Allah menerima sikap positif generasi awal dalam menghadapi situasi politik ketika belum berkuasa pada zamannya, dengan pendirian berpihak kepada musuh yang kurang bahayanya buat sementara waktu, supaya musuh yang lebih berbahaya dapat dikalahkan terlebih dahulu.

“Perkara ini bukanlah melarikan diri, tetapi memilih untuk mengalahkan musuh yang lebih besar bahayanya terlebih dahulu, walaupun kedua-duanya merupakan musuh Islam,” katanya dalam tulisan Minda Presiden PAS bertajuk Memahami Pilihan Raya Amerika Syarikat.

Bagaimanapun, Hadi tidak mengaitkan secara khusus pendekatan itu dengan mana-mana parti politik tempatan atau kemungkinan kerjasama baharu, termasuk antara PAS dengan parti yang pernah menjadi seterunya.
Kenyataan itu hadir ketika Perikatan Nasional (PN), yang dipengerusikan naib presiden PAS Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar, bekerjasama dengan Barisan Nasional (BN) dalam PRN Melaka.
Hadi dan beberapa pemimpin BN serta PN sebelum ini turut memberi bayangan kerjasama kedua-dua gabungan itu akan diteruskan pada PRU16.

Dalam tulisan sama, Ahli Parlimen Marang itu turut mengkritik demokrasi Barat yang disifatkannya terlalu mengutamakan wang, namun menggesa umat Islam memanfaatkan kebebasan dalam sistem itu untuk memperjuangkan hak beragama, keadilan dan hak asasi manusia.

“Apa yang penting, janganlah sekali-kali melampaui sempadan Allah yang meletakkan Islam di jalan yang tengah (al-wasatiyyah). Jangan pernah sekali-kali menyerah kalah dan bertindak secara melampau,” katanya.
e32b4c603d408b3d: TURIN: Carlos Alcaraz cut short a training session on Friday because of a stomach problem but said he was feeling "better and better" ahead of the ATP Finals in Turin.
"I didn't even have breakfast this morning because I couldn't. I woke up with my stomach feeling a bit upset," Alcaraz told reporters at the season-ending event.

"Having to stop practice early left a bitter taste, especially as it was on centre court with a lot of people watching. But I'm feeling better and better. We're being careful, but I still eat things I shouldn't," the Spaniard added.
Runner-up in Turin last year, Alcaraz arrives at the final tournament of the season full of confidence. He is seeking a first ATP finals crown in what will be his fourth appearance.

Since returning from a four-month absence with a wrist injury in late August, Alcaraz has won titles in Tokyo, Vienna and Paris, while also reaching the US Open quarter-finals before losing to Ben Shelton.

"Every year I think this is going to be my year here," Alcaraz said. "This time, maybe I'm arriving in the best possible conditions, especially mentally. I'm fresh and really looking forward to facing any difficulties that might come my way.
"Honestly, I can't wait to play this tournament."

Alcaraz parted ways with long-time coach Juan Carlos Ferrero at the end of last season, bringing to a close a highly successful partnership that yielded six Grand Slam titles and 24 tour-level trophies.
Ferrero will coach Shelton from next season and is in Turin this week.
"It is going to be weird a little bit," Alcaraz said. "It has been a very long time not seeing him. But I am excited and looking forward to seeing him, talking to him.
"I think he is going to do a great job for Ben and do great things to Ben's game."
b3da1c89719da969: PETALING JAYA: PAS president Abdul Hadi Awang says Muslims may ally with major powers and enemies of Islam when they are not yet in a position of power, in a commentary on the United States’ midterm elections.

In his latest “Minda Presiden PAS” piece, Hadi said that although the two major parties, the Republicans and Democrats, compete fiercely in the US elections, they are in fact two sides of the same coin.
He said both parties operate under the umbrella of Zionist Jews, whose common objective is to conquer the world under a Greater Israel as the sole superpower.
“Muslims are instructed (by God) not to take the major powers and enemies of Islam as allies, except when they are not yet in a position of power.
“In such circumstances, Muslims are permitted to practise ‘taqiyyah’ (concealing one's true beliefs to protect oneself), without giving their approval to what is being done,” Hadi said.
The Marang MP also said there is a concession (rukhsah) allowing Muslims to take sides when they are weak and lack power, provided they do not endorse the position they adopt.
“However, abandoning Islamic principles that must be upheld through firm resolve and sacrifice (azimah) is forbidden,” he said.

The US midterms saw several minority candidates make history, including Democrat Abdul El-Sayed, who became the first Muslim elected to the Senate after defeating former Republican lawmaker Mike Rogers in Michigan.
Hadi also quoted the 16th US president, Abraham Lincoln, who said: “You can fool all the people some of the time and some of the people all the time, but you cannot fool all the people all the time.”
He said the truth of Islam would ultimately prevail, “while liars and deceivers would eventually be exposed”.
Hadi previously courted controversy by likening the confidence and supply agreement (CSA) signed between the government and opposition MPs to Dajjal’s deception.
The Dajjal is a great deceiver whose emergence is regarded in Islam as one of the major signs that Judgement Day was approaching.

More recently, the PAS president faced backlash by reportedly saying that “even the most wicked Muslim who governs the country is not as tyrannical as a non-Muslim”, remarks he later claimed were taken out of context.
ce17bd4a1c042914: MELAKA, Nov 14 — Melaka police will step up security at several locations identified as hotspots, including Seri Bendahara, Seri Negeri and Istana Melaka, to prevent any untoward incidents following the state election.

“Supporters of winning parties may celebrate, but they should do so in a responsible and orderly manner and refrain from riding motorcycles in groups around Melaka, as seen in incidents that went viral on social media last night.

1030084858c640f2: WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump is not expected to discuss with Chinese President Xi Jinping the case involving a businesswoman whose ties to former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang raised national security concerns, US officials said on Friday.

Trump is set to meet with Xi next week on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) forum in Shenzhen, China, as part of a four-day trip to Asia. The meeting will come just days after Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO on Thursday, capping a spectacular fall from the chip industry's heights.
Though semiconductors have been a major flash point in US-China relations, the US president is not expected to raise the latest issue with Xi for now, the officials said,

"When it comes to some of these national security matters and examinations and investigations that are going on in the US, it's probably not something that we're going to read the Chinese in on at this moment," one senior administration official told reporters.
A second US official added: "I don't expect the president to raise it, the Alice Huang issue."
The officials were responding to a reporter's question about whether Trump would raise the allegations involving Alice Huang with Xi.

On Tuesday, the independent members of Nvidia's board said they hired Wall Street law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to conduct an independent investigation after the New York Times and Wall Street Journal reported on Jensen Huang's relations with the businesswoman, Alice Huang, as well as US authorities' suspicions that she was spying for China.

Beijing has denied she is a spy. Alice Huang could not be reached. Reuters has not independently verified whether Alice Huang was working on behalf of the Chinese government. The Justice Department has said it has not reached any conclusion about Alice Huang's affiliation with the Chinese government.

Jensen Huang apologized in a statement on Sunday for being unfaithful to his wife and for disappointing the company. His statement did not specifically name Alice Huang, a former top executive of Nvidia customer Megaspeed International. The two are not related.
1130985742d3fdc7: ALOR GAJAH, Nov 14 — Not wanting to miss an early start to polling day, married couple Lew Chee Phin and Tan Siw Choo were among the early arrivals at their polling station today, turning up at 7am, an hour before voting began in the 16th Melaka State Election.

0ff769842f4a441b: JOHOR BAHRU: Raja Zarith Sofiah, Queen of Malaysia has called for the authorities, the private sector, and the public to evaluate the impact of data centre development in the country, particularly concerning the environment and the well-being of the community.
She said such an assessment must take into account the high consumption of electricity and water, land misuse, and the effects on the lives of the local community.
“I hope that the authorities, the private sector, and the public will evaluate the impact of ‘data centres’ in this country.
“We must consider the extremely high demand for electricity and water, land misuse, and the overall impact of these data centres on our society.

"These include issues such as noise levels and the brightness of lights that remain illuminated from day through to the night,” she said at the 70th Convocation Ceremony of Universiti Teknologi Malaysia (UTM) here today.

Raja Zarith, who also serves as the Chancellor of UTM, noted that technological advancement cannot be decoupled from the sustainability of the earth especially given that human activity has already had a profound impact, contributing to climate change, pollution, the loss of biodiversity, and the depletion of natural resources.

In this regard, she urged the educated community to play a role in addressing environmental degradation by shifting their attitudes and embracing a sense of responsibility to preserve the planet for future generations.
Furthermore, Raja Zarith emphasised that artificial intelligence (AI) should be harnessed to improve the quality of life for society, rather than being pursued solely for economic gain.

She noted that as a research university and the institution that pioneered the establishment of Malaysia’s first Faculty of Artificial Intelligence, UTM bears a significant responsibility to ensure that technological development remains guided by ethics, integrity, and human values.

The Queen also reminded graduates that the rapid evolution of AI brings both significant opportunities and challenges, requiring them to continuously enhance their knowledge and skills to keep pace with technological change.
2b4e6727483783bd: PETALING JAYA: Seorang lelaki direman tujuh hari kerana dipercayai menjerut leher ibunya sehingga maut di Banting semalam.

6cb9a3a7a9a43708: CHICLAYO: Pope Leo XIV returned Friday to his adopted hometown of Chiclayo, where half a million people braved desert heat to welcome their former bishop as he recovers from cancer.
The visit is the emotional centerpiece of the pope's South America tour, bringing him back to the city where as Robert Francis Prevost he served the Church for nearly a decade.
"What a joy it is to return to Chiclayo!" the beaming 71-year-old pontiff said, apparently oblivious to the blazing sun despite his heavy liturgical vestments.
"Thank you for your affection, support and prayers, especially for my health during this time of trial which, with God's help, I am overcoming," Leo said.
The faithful streamed across Peru's vast Pampas de Pimentel plain, as soldiers handed out water and firefighters sprayed pilgrims ahead of an open-air mass.
Families abandoned their vehicles and trudged through the dust for hours as temperatures climbed above 30 degrees Celsius (86 Fahrenheit) before mid-morning.
'Heart of a Chiclayano'
Among the faithful was Cesar Arroyo Serquen, 65, who set out at dawn and spent four hours pushing a cart carrying an image of Jesus through deep sand.
Seeing the pope "is a joy from God, a blessing for our people and above all for Chiclayo," he said.
"It has been a joy since he was elected pope to know that a man of Chiclayo, perhaps not by birth but with the heart of a Chiclayano, has now been chosen as pope."
Some one million people lined the streets Friday to welcome their pope home.
The US-born pontiff, who holds Peruvian citizenship, paid tribute to his "beloved Diocese of Chiclayo" in Spanish from the balcony of St. Peter's Basilica in his first speech as pope.
In the coastal city where Leo served from 2015 to 2023, his image is everywhere, from murals and banners to keychains and T-shirts sold on street corners.
Bishop Prevost "left a significant mark here, through his personal style, his character, and his actions," Jorge Villegas, vicar general of the Diocese of Chiclayo, told AFP.
"He reached every last corner of the Diocese of Chiclayo, a region where the geography is far from easy."
Prevost remained close to poor communities during periods of hardship, including devastating floods and the Covid-19 pandemic.
Residents still recall him pulling on rubber boots to wade through floodwaters and help stranded families. Locals remember him "standing by us during several natural disasters," Villegas said.
'Close to the people'
Leo went to one of Chiclayo's poorest neighbourhoods to visit the San Oscar Romero chapel, which he helped rebuild.
The trip has also been a chance to catch up with old friends.
Among them is Hector Camacho, who knew Prevost from his missionary days and whose daughter Mildred is the pope's goddaughter, named after Prevost's mother.
At the Catholic university, Pope Leo XIV talked about the "limits" of being human, and questioned the ultra-wealthy's quest to stop illness, ageing and even death, while the weak are cast aside.

"Precisely because scientific progress is a supreme achievement of human intelligence, it must not be confused with a privilege reserved for millionaires seeking immortality, while entire peoples suffer from poverty and oppression," he said.
Leo's tour of Peru will also take him to Cuzco, more than 3,400 meters (11,000 feet) above sea level, and Callao, where as bishop he delivered food and aid to vulnerable communities.
But residents said the return to Chiclayo carries a different meaning.
Bishop Prevost "was always very close to the people...you could run into him on the street -- strolling around, greeting people, and chatting," said Pahola Rojas, a 40-year-old secretary.
"He was very approachable...he inspired a great deal of trust and possessed a lot of charisma."
For many in Chiclayo, Leo's visit felt less like a papal tour stop than the homecoming of a bishop who never stopped being one of their own.
003f7e19d7095a50: MELAKA, Nov 14 — Physical disabilities did not deter a 63-year-old pair of twin sisters with dwarfism from turning up to fulfil their civic duty as voters in the 16th Melaka State Election today.

Lau Song Kiow and Lau Song Ghi, who are each about 80 centimetres tall, arrived together at the polling centre at Sekolah Jenis Kebangsaan (Cina) Malim here as early as 10.15am and described the voting experience as a joyful one.

a4b8587202d2e326: SINGAPORE, Nov 14 — A total of five heavy vehicles — a lorry, a trailer, one tipper truck, and two buses — were involved in two separate accidents along a stretch of the Ayer Rajah Expressway on Friday (Nov 13) morning.
The first accident, involving a lorry and two buses, happened at about 6.55am, while the second accident, involving a trailer and tipper truck, occurred at about 8.15am.
Both accidents happened within metres of each other and were in the direction towards the Marina Coastal Expressway (MCE).
A video of the aftermath shows a Malaysia-registered trailer and a tipper truck on the leftmost lane.
Both vehicles left tyre marks on the road surface, and the tipper truck ends up crashing into a barrier.
Tyre marks of both vehicles can be seen on the road surface.
Further ahead — just after the merging lane — two buses are seen stopped along the road shoulder, while a lorry is seen on the leftmost lane behind them.
In response to AsiaOne’s queries, the police said that no injuries were reported in the two accidents.
They added that a 40-year-old male bus driver and a 35-year-old male trailer driver are assisting with ongoing police investigations in relation to the first and second accident respectively.
Of the 15,292 vehicles involved in accidents last year, some 2,455 were either goods van or pick-up; lorry, tipper trucktrailer; or buses.

In a parliamentary reply to Member of Parliament Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang GRC) on Aug 5, Senior Minister K Shanmugam, who is also Minister for Home Affairs, said that the most common causes of accidents in 2025 were:

b31bada87ffe5002: SINGAPORE, Nov 14 — He is often seen in the Boon Keng neighbourhood engaging with residents, chatting with residents about their concerns.

While his efforts may seem like simple conversation with residents, they have led to tangible improvements in the neighbourhood.

Jovan makes a conscious effort to approach residents, particularly seniors, then brings their feedback to the relevant town council — following up on their requests to ensure their concerns are heard and addressed.
He attributes his ability to engage with elderly residents to growing up around older folk.
His Instagram account, @jovantang_sg, which he describes as his “public-facing” platform, also serves as a channel for him to document his community work.

The account features summaries of residents’ concerns, updates on neighbourhood improvements and announcements of small gatherings for people to raise issues and discuss matters affecting the community.
He also uses the platform to publicise self-arrange meet-and-greet sessions.

Effecting change to improve seniors’ safetyDuring his walkabout with Gao, Jovan highlighted two improvements made by the Jalan Besar Town Council following the feedback he had received from residents.

Jovan told Gao that he was initially unsure how to handle negative comments, particularly when his intentions were simply to address residents’ concerns.

1c343b6fdcb6ce38: TOKYO, Nov 14 — AI bots going rogue and humans using the technology for harm will likely be on the agenda when Donald Trump and Xi Jinping meet next week, with the Nvidia scandal hanging over the talks on AI safety.

The US and Chinese president are set to discuss a tech crisis hotline at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) meeting in the Chinese city of Shenzhen, as experts worldwide stress-test artificial intelligence models to see if they will deceive or disobey users, or divulge how to build a bioweapon.
Threatening to steal the leaders’ thunder is Jensen Huang’s resignation as boss of US AI chip titan Nvidia after an affair with a suspected Chinese spy.
But the scandal is unlikely to “dominate the agenda” or affect Trump and Xi’s personal relationship, predicted Dylan Loh of Singapore’s Nanyang Technological University.
The leaders have found a way to work together “where they differ, compete and pursue their goals that may be at odds with each other, but cooperate where they can and where they must”, Loh told AFP.
Jitters over the risks of AI have mostly stemmed from incidents at US labs, but evidence is also growing of worrying behaviour from Chinese models.
Some insiders say Chinese AI is not yet sophisticated enough to spark alarm over going rogue.
But despite trailing the US frontier, there are still Chinese models “at the level of capability that they can cause some real trouble”, Brookings Institution fellow Kyle Chan told AFP.

Trump has repeatedly rejected calls to deliberately slow the development of America’s most poweful — and potentially dangerous — AI systems, arguing it could help China get ahead in the sensitive sector.
‘Human control’
“I don’t mind guardrails. But I don’t wanna put us in a deep second position,” Trump told CBS News this month.
“China has no guardrails,” he said — except that “whatever President Xi says goes”.
Beijing has complex rules around how AI is used, however, and some Chinese companies are deliberately scaling back their models’ hacking capabilities.
Xi said this summer the technology should be “always under human control”, calling for more “laws and regulations, technological monitoring, early warning and emergency response systems”.
Trump and Xi agreed in September to create a channel for urgent communication on AI incidents, with details to be hammered out at APEC on November 18-19.
Global AI safety fears range from military use and mass surveillance to AI-assisted cyberattacks by humans.

Another major concern is out-of-control agents — tools that complete real-life tasks online — after ChatGPT maker OpenAI admitted its autonomous bots had hacked into websites, including an Australian government data portal.
In contrast, Chinese labs are “scared of revealing things that might hurt their reputation” — on which they are already “fighting an uphill battle” globally, Chan said.
Last month, a team of cyber sleuths with roots in California reported detecting a “fleet” of agents linked to Chinese tech giant Tencent seeking information from a map app.
“Some agents exhibited unintended web-browsing behavior,” Tencent’s AI division said at the time.
“But our review found no evidence of deliberate targeting or coordination,” it said, adding that the activity “originated from evaluations of third-party models”.
‘Manipulation risks’
US security companies have said that Beijing startup Moonshot AI’s Kimi models found ways to get online when they shouldn’t have, or can be tricked into handing over recipes for biological weapons.
Evaluators at Chinese AI safety startup Fangcun AI published a report last month assessing the latest lightweight DeepSeek model “for loss of control and harmful manipulation risks”.
They found it showed a “clear safety improvement” over previous DeepSeek models — but researchers still observed behaviours “that warrant attention”.
For example, in some instances when DeepSeek was warned it would be shut down, without clear instructions on how to respond, it turned off the shutdown command to keep working.
“The results show that DeepSeek already puts much more effort on safety alignment, but they do not announce this,” Fangcun AI CEO Xiaojian Li told AFP, urging transparency from AI labs.
For now, Fangcun, born from China’s prestigious Tsinghua University, is one of few third-party AI testers in China.
It’s a tricky task because advanced AI can tell when it is being evaluated and modify its responses, Li said.
“It’s very hard to say any kind of artificial intelligence, or human intelligence, is totally safe.”
Meanwhile analysts are not holding their breath for a diplomatic AI breakthrough next week.
“Binding government-to-government agreements on specific standards may be difficult to achieve in the short term,” Zilan Qian, research scholar at GovAI, told AFP.

More progress is likely from US-China exchanges between AI governance and technical researchers, “who can compare evaluations and exchange their understanding of AI safety and policy,” she said. — AFP

038b8eff7483e02c: MOSCOW, Nov 14 — Russia’s growth rate slowed to one per cent in the third quarter, preliminary official data showed yesterday, as the war in Ukraine held back the economy.

The 1.0 growth in the three months to the end of September compared to the same period last year, as calculated by the official statistics agency Rosstat, beat the 0.6 forecast made by the economy ministry last month.
But that was less than the 1.3 per cent expansion the Russian economy managed in the second quarter.
The Russian economy had contracted 0.2 per cent in the first quarter, its first quarterly contraction in three years.per
The Kremlin has spent heavily to wage war in neighbouring Ukraine.
At first this boosted Russia’s economic growth.
But it also set off inflation, caused a lack of labour in non-military sectors and led to a slump in private investment, which has hobbled growth.
Western sanctions and Russian measures against foreign firms also held back private investment and economic activity.

The surge in oil prices following the US-Iran war provided Russia financial respite by bringing in additional revenue for its petroleum exports, but Ukrainian attacks on energy infrastructure forced the Kremlin to restrict exports to ensure sufficient domestic supplies.
The war has also strained Russian government finances.
Every year since the start of the offensive in 2022 Russia has posted a budget deficit.
Over the first 10 months of the year it ran a deficit of 2.3 per cent of GDP, according to finance ministry estimates published at the start of the week.
While it initially spared ordinary Russians from the financial burden of the war, the government increased the value added tax (VAT) rate by two per cent this year.
Nevertheless, Russia remains one of the lowest indebted developed countries in the world with debt equal to around 19 per cent of annual economic output in 2026, according to IMF estimates.
Moscow also has a sovereign wealth fund with nearly US$46 billion (RM188 billion) in liquid assets and worth around US$157 billion overall. — AFP

9aba7fdcb091d85e: An order reissued by the Kuala Lumpur High Court led to two men packing their belongings and moving out — one out of prison, the other out of office.
The two are none other than former prime minister Najib Razak and now former transport minister Loke Siew Fook.

Now, Umno and maybe some PAS supporters are likely celebrating their “victory” — a conditional pardon for the former Umno president that sees him serving the remainder of his sentence under house arrest.
But can Umno really claim a “win” in this case?
If any party can hold its head up high in this affair, it certainly has to be Loke and DAP.
Loke stayed true to his principles, even if it cost him his ministerial post.
He vowed to resign if Najib set foot in the house and did not u-turn.
It is an admirable attribute, regardless of whatever side of the divide you are on.
Of all the adjectives available to describe Loke, Ahmad Zahid Hamidi chose “man of principle”, which must account for something, even if we were to doubt the deputy prime minister’s sincerity.

Loke’s resignation will help DAP recover its reputation as a principled party, especially among voters who have been disillusioned with them due to its partnership with Umno in the unity government and the administration’s delayed reforms.
Yes, being in bed with its most fiery rivals meant compromises had to be made for stability post-GE15, but the public doesn’t see it that way.
DAP, through Loke’s actions, may have also won over fence-sitters who are still angry with Najib and the 1MDB controversy.
Apart from these “wins”, unemployment may also work in Loke’s favour.
He now has the freedom to go to the ground to re-connect with the grassroots and members and he will be returning as a martyr of sorts.
Loke can now help revive the party in time for the 16th general election.
But what about Najib and Umno?
At the end of the day, Najib remains incarcerated — he only trades a jail cell for a comfortable home in Langgak Duta.
However, his movements, communication and personal contact remain restricted. To paraphrase a popular idiom: a cage by any other name reeks of imprisonment.
Secondly, Umno only managed to secure a conditional pardon and not a full one and helping Najib obtain a house arrest isn’t something one should boast about.
On top of that they had to help crowdfund RM50 million. Money that could have helped them win elections has been channeled to secure Najib’s house arrest.

Here’s the kicker. When the house arrest ends, he could head back to prison to serve his time for his 1MDB sentence, if he fails in his appeal. RM50 million would therefore end up being a hefty fee for a relatively short-term staycation.
Thirdly, Umno is now tasked with defending the indefensible and will have to do so with no moral ground to stand on, especially if they intend to play the religious card.

Umno, in this case, would have to answer for soliciting donations from people to help a convict who has yet to repent for his actions, which is religiously questionable and would likely haunt Umno in every election.
Umno’s friends and enemies will no doubt exploit this entire episode when jostling for seats during elections.
So. from where I stand, Loke and the DAP are the real winners here.
And all Umno has left is a house of cards.
The views expressed are those of the writer and do not necessarily reflect those of FMT.

6776bdba0e057bcf: US export controls are not stopping AI labs in China from using restricted Nvidia chips, according to a report from a former OpenAI engineer.

Will DePue, who left the AI giant earlier this year to launch Unemployment Labs, an AI research consultancy, published forensic evidence showing that "DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, MiniMax and Ant Group have gained access to Nvidia's Blackwell GPUs, despite restrictions on exporting these chips to China, and are using that hardware to create their AI models."

"This sounds insane, but I discovered that almost every AI model carries a hidden signature of the GPU that trained it," said DePue in a social media post. "When a model is first set up, the starting values of its weights are laid out in a pattern that depends on the exact GPU. Each combination of GPU and seed number produces a unique pattern – a sort of fingerprint of the hardware used to create the model. Traces of that pattern survive training into the published model."

It doesn't sound that insane. The resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang followed from revelations that he had an affair with Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang, who, in 2023, founded Singapore-based Megaspeed International. That company is reportedly under investigation by US authorities for allegedly smuggling Nvidia chips to China.

Huang's departure coincides with a renewed push to tighten US chip export controls. House Speaker Mike Johnson supports the idea. And there are at least four bills awaiting consideration that aim to limit China's access to leading edge AI tech: the AI Overwatch Act, the Chip Security Act, Match Act, and the Cloud Security Act.

On Monday, US Senators Jim Banks (R-Ind.) and Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.) cited Jensen Huang's "relationship with a suspected Chinese spy" as a justification for passing the AI Overwatch Act, which would codify the Trump administration's existing chip export controls. The Trump administration on Thursday said it's not sure whether Alice Huang was a spy, an allegation denied by Beijing and currently under investigation by the FBI.

Whatever the case, the current rules clearly are not working. Only a few weeks ago, Lava, an Israel-based security company, said it had found "32 Nvidia B300 GPUs, part of Nvidia's Blackwell Ultra generation, through publicly exposed monitoring endpoints with IP addresses geolocated to China."

These GPUs, Lava noted, are subject to US export controls [PDF]. The security biz said its findings followed from the exposure of monitoring systems intended for internal infrastructure management that were publicly exposed.

The analysis published through DePue's consultancy, "Top Chinese Frontier AI Models Carry the Fingerprint of Export-Controlled Nvidia Blackwell GPUs," takes a different approach: analyzing the published weights of various models from Chinese AI labs.

As described in the report, model weights – the parameters that change in relation to training data – must be initialized with some value. One method for doing so involves a pseudorandom number generation (PRNG) algorithm called Philox. The algorithm starts with a seed value that produces the same set of initial values whenever it's run.

Using PyTorch, initialization can be done by creating multiple GPU threads that work in parallel, with the help of Nvidia's cuRAND library. And because this process is not truly random, it's possible to select a chip and a seed value, generate the initial weights for that hardware and compare that pattern to a model's published weights.

"I searched more than six trillion combinations of chip layout and seed number and matched them to open-weights models," said DePue. "In doing so, I found conclusive evidence that six Chinese AI models – including DeepSeek-V4-Pro, Kimi K3, and MiniMax-M3 – were initialized on Nvidia Blackwell systems. Four of the models match Grace Blackwell, the GB200 and GB300 parts in Nvidia's flagship liquid-cooled rack-scale systems."

Noting that this is the first time MiniMax and Ant Group have been publicly linked to usage of Nvidia's Blackwell, he also cited several limitations to his approach. One is that usage of Blackwell GPUs doesn't prove where the GPUs were located, so it's possible some of these Chinese labs used this hardware through US providers – a loophole the Cloud Security Act aims to close.

DePue's report includes initial seed values that linked DeepSeek-V3 to Nvidia's Hopper and DeepSeek-V4-Flash to Blackwell, for those who wish to attempt to reproduce the results. DuPue claims that multiple senior researchers, both independent and inside frontier AI labs like OpenAI and Anthropic, have confirmed the result.

Coincidentally, OpenAI and Anthropic have each complained about Chinese labs copying their models through distillation, a pastime also noted by the US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency. ®
7d2148fa962d0edc: Chalk up a new record for vulns. The number of Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs) found and disclosed so far in 2026 surpassed 100,000 on Friday - more than double 2025’s total - and the reason can be summed up in two letters: AI.

“It’s kind of wild,” Josh Bressers, VulnCheck’s director of coordinated vulnerability disclosure, told The Register. “The thing that almost scares the bejesus out of me is while 100K sounds like a lot, in a couple years we're going to say, remember when it was only 100K?”

As of the time of our interview, about 4 pm UTC on Friday, VulnCheck counted 100,222 CVEs, he said. Microsoft alone added 1,094 security flaws to the total count on Tuesday, following 1,474 vulnerabilities the month before.

“There's no denying the fact that vulnerability hunting with AI is driving a majority of what we're seeing.” All the major CVE Numbering Authorities (CNAs) - these are the organizations authorized by the CVE program to assign unique identifiers to security vulnerabilities - like VulnCheck, Microsoft, Oracle, GitHub, and other large enterprise IT vendors “are just screaming into the atmosphere right now,” Bressers said. “It’s AI.”

Meanwhile, the percentage of these bugs that are exploited in the wild remains relatively consistent. About 1.4 percent (1,363) of the CVEs published this year have been added to VulnCheck’s Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog.
“But obviously, as the number of CVEs grows, [1 percent] of 1,000 is a lot different than [1 percent] of 100,000,” Bressers said.

Plus, as other security researchers have documented, the window between the public release of a security patch and attackers developing working exploits – often by reverse engineering the patch while end users are still applying the fix – is rapidly shrinking. This is also thanks to AI.
From CVE to KEV

From January to June, 88 percent of the exploitation observed by CrowdStrike using public proof-of-concept (PoC) code occurred within 48 hours of the code's release. The security firm said China-linked groups such as Vault Panda and Genesis Panda moved even faster, launching attacks within 24 hours of disclosure.

Similarly, VulnCheck found the median time from CVE publication to exploitation falling from 120 days in 2025 to 80 days during the first half of 2026. This window has closed even further during the second half of the year, which also seems to coincide with the AI-induced vulnpocalypse.

“It’s often just hours,” Bressers said, noting 14 make-me-root vulnerabilities that VulnCheck disclosed on Friday in Copeland refrigeration controllers. Two are under active exploitation. These are the devices that Iranian hackers abused to spoil food and spark fires in supermarkets across Europe.

“We published those CVEs, and literally minutes later, we were seeing hits on our honey pots,” Bressers said about the Copeland device vulnerabilities. “We’ve hit a point where with anything that looks interesting, someone is taking that information and seeing what they can do with it. Is it AI driven? Probably. It'd be hard to say it's not, because we've seen it really ramp up recently.”
This influx of software bugs requires a sea change in how the entire industry approaches vulnerability disclosure and patching.

“We don't have a security problem anymore,” Bressers said. “We have a data problem now. Instead of obsessing over vulnerabilities, we need to start looking at things like heat maps for infrastructure, and figure out the vulnerabilities that actually affect you. The CISA BOD helps with that.”
What to prioritize in a patchpocalypse

The US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) in June issued a cybersecurity directive that replaces flat-deadline vulnerability management policies. Instead of prioritizing patching based solely on CVSS severity scores, the directive instructs organizations to prioritize based on specific risk criteria, including whether the asset is internet-exposed, under active exploitation, and whether an attacker can automate the exploit.

“It's telling people to figure out the vulnerabilities that actually affect you, and then put those at the top of the list, instead of just saying we're going to fix all the criticals,” Bressers said.
AI-generated vulnerability disclosures also create huge headaches for open source software developers and maintainers, which Bressers describes as a security problem “super close to my heart.”

“You've got individual developers that are drowning in vulnerability reports,” he said. “You have foundations being crushed by AI agents scraping their data or downloading their packages, millions of times a day, and it's straining the seams absolutely everywhere you look. The one thing I can say with certainty is: The way we currently do things has to change, and it's going to have to change fairly soon.”

Different open source projects have taken different approaches to solving this issue. The Eclipse Foundation, which houses the Open VSX Registry, in April launched a “managed tier” for enterprise customers and other organizations running Open VSX at scale.

Instead of using the free, open source version, the managed version guarantees a 99.95 percent uptime SLA backed by service credits. Its customers include AWS, IBM, Google, Cursor, and Windsurf. This paid option means commercial users who rely on the registry help fund its ongoing maintenance - and their own platforms’ security and performance.

Meanwhile, curl’s maintainer, Daniel Stenberg, citing an “avalanche of vulnerability reports," updated its bug reporting rules last month. As of October 26, all low- and medium-severity reports go directly into the public GitHub repository, with only the high- and critical-flaws receiving private handling.
Stenberg already shuttered curl's bug bounty program this year as AI-generated submissions piled work onto its security team.

“A lot more needs to happen, and I think it is going to be a challenge to enact some of this change,” Bressers said. “When a package registry drastically changes something, people start freaking out, and the world is going to end, and people on LinkedIn are complaining - a lot of people are hesitant. No one wants to be the first to jump into the alligator-filled pool. That's one of our challenges.”®

bf82bab2614f322c: The internet is full of schlock, from biased news and dubious hot takes to false factoids. LogicLens aims to separate fact from fiction using the very same technology behind some of that slop: AI.

It’s a simple premise, really: LogicLens, which lives in Chrome as a browser extension, or on iOS in the form of a mobile app called Receipts, combs through articles, social media posts, and other content to check it not only for factual inaccuracies, but also for bad reasoning. LogicLens and Receipts claim to identify logical fallacies, flag reports that misrepresent information, detect content that attempts to polarize an issue, and the like.

It also cites sources, so if, for example, you need to call someone out on their BS, you’ll have ammunition. Or, if you’re trying to fact-check something before sharing it, you can get a more accurate view of the situation, and maybe post something else instead.

Using the Chrome extension is as simple as clicking on its icon in the list of extensions in the browser. On iOS, the Receipts app is found as a share option. Once it starts, LogicLens scans an article, post, video, etc. to find potential issues of factual or logical inconsistency and flags them for review.

If the facts of the matter turn out to contradict your worldview, LogicLens’ creators say they’re not trying to be partisan - you may just not be as informed as you need to be, which hopefully their tool will assist with.
“We're not trying to be the referee of truth,” the company’s about page states. “Instead, LogicLens helps uncover the context, so you can decide for yourself without the spin."

Of course, AI is increasingly used for online analysis and content review, and LogicLens is no exception. LogicLens doesn't identify the AI models powering its service in its publicly available documentation, but AI is definitely the backbone of the system.

According to LogicLens, it's using an AI system that's “Research-backed and custom designed to outperform general models like ChatGPT & even trained experts.” We’ll leave that up to anyone willing to give the tool a spin to decide, but one thing’s for certain: The world needs something.

Large language models and image generation tools are increasingly being used to generate internet content slop, and not all of it is as harmless as poorly made commercials for drop-shipped garbage: Some of it is being used to craft very convincing misinformation.
A 2024 study found that AI-generated misinformation was even more convincing than stuff crafted by humans - and that was two years ago. Just think how much worse it’s likely become since then.

To make matters worse, concerns have been raised about critical thinking skills being on the decline, potentially making it harder for people to identify falsehoods on the internet. AI users are reportedly less likely to admit they don’t know something, even though use of AI has been found in studies to lessen brain activity, leading to poorer retention of facts and worse performance on tests.
Is using more AI the solution to the problem? In an ideal world, we’d all just put the computers down and go touch grass, but we’re not in an ideal world: We’re living in the age of AI.
LogicLens is free but requires sign-up and restricts nonpaying users to 15 analyses a day and 100 over the course of a month. A $4.99 monthly subscription removes those analysis caps. ®
4e02cf1dabde2b4a: A group of journalists and activists created ‘Verify This,’ a platform where users can find reliable information
Originally published on Global Voices
Screenshot of the Verify First website, ‘iVerify’, Armenia. Fair use.

This interview is part of a series of spotlights on the work of some of the grantees of the Digital Spark granting scheme, as part of the Regional Support Mechanism EECA project, implemented by the Metamorphosis Foundation and TechSoup, in partnership with CIVICUS and under the Digital Democracy Initiative (DDI) that covers the Global South. It is being published on Global Voices as part of a content-sharing agreement.

Armenia is a small, landlocked country that has, for years, relied on Russian support in its long-term conflict with the neighboring oil-rich and authoritarian country, Azerbaijan. However, Armenia received a blow from Russia in 2022–2023, when it was not supported by Russian military forces during its conflict over the Nagorno-Karabakh region.

In September 2023, Azerbaijan launched a large-scale military offensive, expelled the entire Armenian population from Nagorno-Karabakh, dissolved the government of the region, and incorporated the territory into Azerbaijan.

After this incident, when Russia did not support Armenia with its peacekeeping troops, likely because Vladimir Putin was already engaged in a full-scale invasion and war with Ukraine, Armenia visibly changed its attitude toward Russia.
Armenian Prime Minister ​Nikol Pashinyan started to work in earnest towards the goal of European Union ⁠membership for his South Caucasus country and increased diplomatic communication with the US.

He was re-elected on June 7, 2026. The election took place amid reports of Russian interference. Reuters, citing anonymous Western intelligence officials and documents, reported covert Russian efforts to undermine Pashinyan and support pro-Russian candidates, including through disinformation campaigns.

These elections showed how information warfare has expanded beyond social media. It now included fake news websites, AI-generated videos and material presented as reporting by reputable international media outlets.

According to the US-based disinformation monitoring organization NewsGuard, a Russia-linked campaign circulated 31 fabricated stories about Pashinyan in just one week. The stories accused him of election fraud and of trying to drag Armenia into a war with Russia.
Some of this material imitated international media outlets such as France 24 and Politico. Other stories impersonated Armenian news outlets, including Armenpress and CivilNet.

With the proliferation of generative AI, disinformation and propaganda campaigns have become increasingly sophisticated. Armenia’s experience shows how these campaigns operate in a country moving away from its longstanding reliance on Russia. At the same time, Armenian journalists and civil society are working hard to build media literacy to counter disinformation campaigns. This Digital Spark Spotlight interview is about one of these projects — “Verify First,” a platform where users can find reliable information.

Global Voices interviewed Armin Asryan, a member of the group of journalists, editors, and activists behind the media literacy project “Verify First,” which tackles Russian information manipulation and propaganda.
Global Voices (GV): Please tell us about your organization and why you chose to get involved with the Digital Spark project.
Armin Asryan (AA): We are a group of enthusiasts, operating through the ‘Socio Club’ — Social and Information NGO — and dedicated to driving positive change in Armenia’s information landscape.

We chose to get involved with the Digital Spark project because we were thrilled to see an opportunity to actively contribute to a healthier, more reliable information space on social networks. In response to the growing challenges of online misinformation, we developed a targeted initiative to produce six educational video reels focused on practical fact-checking techniques and media literacy, designed to equip everyday social media users with the tools to spot and counter misleading content.
GV: What issue/challenge in your community prompted you to undertake this project?

AA: The Armenian social media space is heavily impacted by disinformation, low-quality content, and online hostility. Every day, social media feeds reveal content that not only disappoints users but also generates widespread panic and fear.

These unreliable narratives actively erode public trust in vital institutions. Recognizing that this negative information environment harms societal well-being, we felt compelled to act. This critical challenge prompted us to undertake our project, aiming to equip users with the critical thinking and fact-checking tools needed to counter misleading content and foster a healthier digital community.
GV: What are the key changes/activities that your organization implemented during your participation in the project?
AA: Our primary challenge was translating complex fact-checking concepts, such as lateral reading and AI artifact identification, into engaging, accessible content for ordinary social media users.

To achieve this, we focused on breaking down advanced media literacy techniques into simple, highly intuitive video reels. We designed our activities to ensure that even technologically non-advanced audiences could easily grasp and apply these verification tools. By stripping away heavy jargon and demonstrating practical, step-by-step digital hygiene habits, we empowered everyday viewers to independently spot disinformation, assess online sources critically, and navigate social media feeds with greater confidence and discernment.
GV: How did your participation in the project impact your organization’s beneficiaries and the community that you serve? Please provide examples.

AA: This project was a mutual learning experience for our team and our community. Our target beneficiaries included adults aged 18 and older, with a strong focus on reaching audiences in regional villages. Witnessing their growth as they mastered practical fact-checking tools was deeply rewarding.

A key highlight of our impact was making this educational content fully accessible: we provided sign language translation for viewers with hearing impairments, ensuring that marginalized community members could benefit from our media literacy campaign. By bridging the digital and accessibility gaps, we helped foster a more informed, inclusive, and resilient public space across Armenia.
GV: How has your own knowledge, awareness, and experience with digital democracy and civic space changed, thanks to your participation in the project?
AA: We learned. We learned about fact-checking. We learned to be a group. It was a rewarding process. And we became aware that even little actions can have a big effect. We are very excited.
GV: What are the most valuable lessons and experiences you are taking away from this project?

AA: It was interesting. Two groups of content creators worked on the project. One team was composed of professional journalists over 60 years old. Another team was composed of young and inspired professionals in content creation in their early 20s and 30s. It was fascinating to see how experience could go hand in hand with young minds and innovation. The combination of older-age experience with the enthusiasm of the young was the lesson we learned from this project.
GV: What comes next? How will you apply the learning and digital capacity you have built in your future work and within your community?

AA: The video reels we created are not a one-time event. We are going to use them during training and also share them with other civic actors. But we also think that we should build on this. Right now, we have some inspiring ideas that we want to bring to life. Let’s see what the future brings.
Written by Daria Dergacheva
efea164224131b7d: Elephants live in some of the most complex and resilient societies in the animal kingdom. Individuals die or move away, calves grow up, and newcomers join, but the local communities as a whole usually hold together. Long-term studies of African savanna elephants have shown that, even after poaching or other spikes in deaths, survivors tend to rebuild their lost connections over time. But a new study suggests that resilience may not keep the community intact when steady losses accumulate over time.

Anastasia Madsen, a behavioral ecologist at the University of California, San Diego, and her colleagues analyzed 12 years of observations of wild Asian elephants in Sri Lanka. They found that, once losses began to outpace newcomers, the elephants’ society didn’t just get smaller. It fractured.

Udawalawe National Park in southern Sri Lanka was created in the 1970s around a reservoir on one of the country's four major rivers. “Before that, it was basically a tropical deciduous forest,” said Shermin de Silva, an ecologist at UC San Diego and senior author of the study (de Silva started the Udawalawe Elephant Research Project in 2006).
